items.title: Fury reveals schizophrenia diagnosis
items.description: Tyson Fury says he was diagnosed with schizophrenia soon after his world title win over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015. British heavyweight Fury, 38, says he heard voices in his head threatening to hurt him and his family. In a documentary which will be released by Netflix on Friday, Fury and wife Paris describe how he was diagnosed after being admitted to hospital with a suspected heart attack in June 2016. “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” Fury says. “It was like a living version of the pits of hell. I thought I would end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much. “The anxiety was crippling me. I just could not overcome it and that’s when I went and saw the psychiatrist down in London. She asked me a gazillion questions, and I ticked all the boxes. Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder.” Doctors said Fury had suffered an anxiety attack. Fury recalls hearing the radio talking to him, and begging Paris to get him out of the hospital because “the Illuminati” wanted him. In the period after his victory over Klitschko, Fury gained weight and struggled with drug and alcohol addiction. “It got that bad I was hearing voices in my mind,” he says. “I wouldn’t be able to sit and have a conversation because I’d be hearing stuff in my mind. “I didn’t know where to turn and no-one knew what to do. I really needed help, or check into rehab or something. “I never got a break from it for years. I wanted to be what I thought was normal again.” After Fury was released from hospital, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder was confirmed, according to the documentary. The NHS describes schizophrenia, external as a form of psychosis, and symptoms can include hallucinations, delusions and muddled thoughts and speech. It says the main symptom of bipolar disorder, external is extreme changes to your mood. Fury describes a “turning point” in 2017 when he was on a night out for Halloween. “I went out and I was embarrassed by how I looked,” he says. “I was a fat mess and I had a glow-in-the-dark skeleton suit with full face mask on. “I looked around and could see all the young people and I thought, ‘I had the world in my hands and I threw it all away, and now I’m a fat mess addicted to alcohol’.” He says that was the beginning of a comeback which led him to focus more on his family and to return to training. It resulted in another world title when he beat Deontay Wilder in 2020. Fury is preparing for the long-awaited all-British heavyweight fight against Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on 11 December. The fight will be broadcast live on Netflix.

items.title: Rent Control considers easing six-month rent advance restriction
items.description: Landlords in Ghana could be allowed to collect up to 12 months’ rent in advance under a proposed amendment to the country’s rent law, a move that has already drawn opposition from tenant advocates. The proposal, being considered by the Rent Control Department, would double the current six-month limit stipulated under the Rent Act, 1963 (Act 220), for tenancies exceeding six months. Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, disclosed this on JoyNews’ The Probe programme on Sunday, November 22, 2026, explaining that the proposal followed repeated concerns from property owners about the financial demands of developing and maintaining rental accommodation. He said landlords had argued during stakeholder engagements that the existing restriction did not adequately reflect the cost of property investment and the resources required to keep buildings in good condition. Mr Opoku stressed, however, that the proposed change was still at the drafting stage and had not received ministerial approval. It would have to go through the necessary executive and legislative processes, including consideration by Cabinet and Parliament, before it could become law. Under Section 25(5) of Act 220, a landlord is prohibited from demanding more than six months’ rent in advance where the tenancy is for a period exceeding six months. The proposed revision would therefore represent a significant change to the existing arrangement, which has become a contentious issue in Ghana’s rental market. Tenants raise concerns The National Tenants Union has questioned the need to extend the advance payment period when, in its view, authorities have struggled to enforce the existing law. A representative of the union, Reindolph Afrifa-Oware, said the immediate priority should be to ensure compliance with the current six-month limit rather than introduce a provision that could increase the financial pressure on tenants. He said some landlords were already demanding one year’s rent in advance, despite the legal restriction, while tenants in parts of Kumasi were reportedly being asked to pay as much as two years’ rent upfront. Mr Afrifa-Oware called for increased investment in the Rent Control Department to strengthen its capacity to monitor landlords, enforce tenancy regulations and protect renters from excessive advance payment demands. He warned that allowing a longer period could worsen the difficulties facing tenants, particularly those who struggle to raise large sums before securing accommodation. Landlords defend proposal For his part, Emmanuel Preko-Boamah, representing the national secretariat of the Voice of Landlords Association in Ghana, said rent regulations must also recognise the financial obligations property owners face. He argued that the cost of constructing, financing and maintaining residential properties should be taken into account in any review of the law. Mr Preko-Boamah also appealed to the government to reduce or absorb some of the administrative charges landlords incur when accessing services from the Rent Control Department. The debate highlights the competing concerns of property owners seeking to recover their investments and tenants struggling with the high upfront cost of securing accommodation. For now, the proposed 12-month limit remains subject to further consideration and approval, while the existing six-month restriction under Act 220 remains the applicable legal requirement.

items.title: Féguiboxe : Boubacar Biro Barry dénonce l’inaction du Ministère des Sports et alerte sur une possible suspension
items.description: Le contentieux opposant Alpha Amadou Baldé à Boubacar Biro Barry, qui se réclament tous deux de la présidence de la Fédération guinéenne de boxe (Féguiboxe), se poursuit devant la justice. À la sortie du tribunal ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, Boubacar Biro Barry a dénoncé l’inaction du Ministère des Sports, estimant que ce différend aurait dû être réglé par les autorités sportives. Il met également en garde contre les conséquences d’une crise qui, selon lui, pourrait conduire à la suspension de la fédération par les instances internationales. Le bras de fer autour de la présidence de la Fédération guinéenne de boxe (Féguiboxe) continue de se jouer devant les tribunaux. À l’issue de l’audience de ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, Boubacar Biro Barry, qui revendique lui aussi la direction de cette fédération, a exprimé son regret de voir ce contentieux sportif prendre une tournure judiciaire. Face aux médias, il a affirmé que cette affaire dure depuis deux ans et demi, malgré les démarches entreprises auprès du Ministère des Sports pour trouver une solution. « Nous sommes au tribunal aujourd’hui pour un contentieux qui dure deux ans et demi. Nous avons approché le Ministère, ça fait deux ans et demi. Aujourd’hui, on se retrouve au tribunal par l’inaction de ce département », a-t-il déclaré, avant de réaffirmer sa position sur la nature du différend. « Nous continuons à penser que ce problème n’a pas sa place au tribunal, mais au Ministère des Sports », a-t-il insisté. Un différend lié à la gouvernance de la fédération Interrogé sur les faits qui lui sont reprochés dans cette procédure, Boubacar Biro Barry a évoqué un contentieux lié à la vie institutionnelle de la fédération, notamment à une assemblée générale. Selon lui, les problèmes soulevés relèvent de la Loi L018 régissant le sport en Guinée et devraient être traités par les autorités compétentes du secteur. Il estime ainsi que le Ministère des Sports ne devrait pas rester en retrait face aux difficultés de gouvernance qui affectent les fédérations sportives nationales. « Il est inacceptable que le Ministère s’arrête et laisse de tels agissements se dérouler dans le monde du sport », a-t-il dénoncé. Dans la même intervention, Boubacar Biro Barry a déploré ce qu’il considère comme une différence de traitement entre le football et les autres disciplines sportives en Guinée. « Nous ne sommes pas le football. C’est vrai, c’est le plus grand sport en Guinée. Tous les problèmes du football sont résolus en deux minutes. Les problèmes des autres fédérations prennent cinq ans, dix ans à être résolus. Ce n’est pas acceptable », a-t-il regretté. Boubacar Biro Barry réclame une nouvelle assemblée générale Pour sortir de cette crise, le responsable sportif appelle le Ministère des Sports à prendre ses responsabilités et à organiser une assemblée générale sous sa supervision, afin que les membres statutaires puissent départager les deux protagonistes. Boubacar Biro Barry affirme avoir toujours réclamé cette démarche, se disant convaincu de disposer de la majorité au sein de la fédération. « Nous avons la majorité. Nous sommes tellement sûrs que nous avons la majorité que ça fait deux ans et demi qu’on demande au Ministère d’organiser une assemblée qu’ils vont superviser, à laquelle Monsieur Baldé et moi allons participer pour que les membres statutaires nous départagent », a-t-il expliqué. Il a également rappelé que le Ministère leur aurait demandé d’attendre le 20 janvier 2026, date qu’il présente comme l’échéance de leur mandat, avant de prendre une décision définitive. « Le 20 janvier est arrivé, ils n’ont rien fait », a-t-il déploré, évoquant des engagements qui auraient été pris par le Directeur National Adjoint des Sports et le Secrétaire Général du Ministère. Malgré ces démarches, Boubacar Biro Barry affirme que la situation reste bloquée. Il assure toutefois faire tout son possible pour éviter un incident au sein de cette fédération de sport de combat. Une possible suspension de la Féguiboxe en toile de fond Au-delà du différend judiciaire, Boubacar Biro Barry redoute des conséquences plus importantes pour la boxe guinéenne. Selon lui, la persistance de cette crise pourrait exposer la Féguiboxe à une suspension par les instances internationales. « Les conséquences de ça peuvent être la suspension pure et simple de la Fédération guinéenne de boxe par les instances internationales », a-t-il alerté. Il estime que les conflits opposant une fédération nationale à une confédération ou à des instances internationales ne devraient pas être débattus dans le cadre d’une procédure judiciaire nationale. Alors que les deux protagonistes continuent de se réclamer de la présidence de la Féguiboxe, l’issue de cette procédure reste attendue, dans un contexte où la crise de gouvernance fait peser des incertitudes sur l’avenir de la boxe guinéenne. items.title: Raya to miss Dortmund game but injury ‘not serious’
items.description: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya’s shoulder injury “doesn’t look too serious”, but he will miss Tuesday’s Champions League against Borussia Dortmund, says Mikel Arteta. Raya was helped off the pitch in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday. He hurt his left shoulder while claiming a cross and making contact with Newcastle forward William Osula. “We need some more tests [on Tuesday] but it is quite encouraging,” said Gunners boss Arteta. “He is not fit [to face Dortmund] but it doesn’t look too serious.” Arteta said that while the incident looked pretty innocuous the pain his keeper was in made him fear it was a serious injury. “With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected,” said Arteta. “When you look at the action it doesn’t seem to be much but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying. “We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment. “The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let’s see.” Arsenal face Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City , Brentford , Tottenham Hotspur and Real Madrid in their next tranche of matches. And Raya is huge part of the way that Arsenal play because of his ability with the ball at his feet. When asked if losing Raya for a long period of time would be the biggest blow to his team, Arteta said: “We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protective with Kepa [Arrizabalaga] and Illan [Meslier]. “Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have in Kepa and Illan.”

items.title: De Bruyne’s feelings for Man City will ‘never change’
items.description: Kevin de Bruyne says his feelings for Manchester City will “never change” even if the club are stripped of their titles after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules. De Bruyne, 35, enjoyed a trophy-laden decade at Etihad Stadium, lifting 16 trophies including the Treble in 2023 before leaving on a free transfer to join Napoli in 2025. The Belgian returns to City for the second time on Tuesday when Napoli play them in the Champions League. De Bruyne says he has “nothing but affection” for the club and that “will never change” even if City were forced to give up their domestic titles. “Of course, it’s a lot of things that’s been going on, but I cannot change anything about that. I am proud of what I have done as a football player and, honestly, this is my club,” he said. “I love the owners; I have talked about a lot of stuff outside football – I have even spoken to [chairman] Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] about how to buy a club.” City deny any wrongdoing and are appealing the decision. In September it was revealed that an independent commission found that City had arranged “sham contracts” with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than £830m. ‘Everybody plays on the limits’ City await any sanctions that may be imposed following their guilty verdict, with possible punishments ranging from a hefty fine, points deductions, relegation from the Premier League and being stripped of titles. Asserting its innocence, City said it had filed “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence [that] exists in support of all of its positions” on 2 October. Sources have told BBC Sport that City were expected to claim that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, as part of an appeal. Criticism of City has been intense, but De Bruyne said he can’t “change anything” about people calling his former club a “disgrace”. “Of course, in life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit, I would say, and for me, I played in between the white lines,” he said. “I don’t think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played, but everybody has their own opinion.” De Bruyne will receive a generous ovation when he returns to Etihad Stadium, having played more than 400 games for City and scoring 108 goals. After his final home game for the club in May 2025, it was announced that a statue will be built in his honour outside the stadium.

items.title: Guinée : le FMI valide un programme de 425 millions de dollars pour la période 2026-2029
items.description: Le Conseil d’administration du Fonds monétaire international (FMI) a approuvé, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, un programme économique et financier triennal en faveur de la Guinée, pour un montant d’environ 425 millions de dollars américains. Soutenu par la Facilité élargie de crédit (FEC) et le Mécanisme élargi de crédit (MEDC), cet accord porte sur un montant exact de 310,59 millions de droits de tirage spéciaux (DTS). Il vise notamment à consolider les réformes de la gestion des finances publiques, à améliorer la transparence budgétaire et à accroître la mobilisation des recettes intérieures. Selon le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, ce programme constitue également un levier important pour accompagner la mise en œuvre du vaste programme de développement Simandou 2040. Un label de crédibilité pour rassurer les investisseurs Au terme de négociations qu’il a qualifiées d’« âpres », le Premier ministre, Amadou Oury Bah, a salué un « alignement des planètes ». Pour le chef du gouvernement, la portée de cet accord va bien au-delà de l’enveloppe financière mobilisée. Il représente surtout un signal de confiance adressé aux investisseurs et aux partenaires financiers internationaux. « La signature du FMI est extrêmement importante pour tout pays ouvert qui veut faire progresser son économie », a-t-il déclaré. Selon lui, ce partenariat avec l’institution de Bretton Woods permettra à la Guinée de renforcer sa crédibilité financière, de mobiliser des financements à des conditions plus avantageuses et de créer un environnement plus rassurant pour les investissements, notamment dans le cadre du mégaprojet minier de Simandou. L’expertise technique du FMI au cœur des attentes Au-delà des ressources financières, les autorités guinéennes comptent également sur l’accompagnement technique et institutionnel du FMI pour améliorer le pilotage de l’économie nationale et moderniser la gouvernance publique. « Nous avons besoin de l’œil du FMI, non pas simplement pour obtenir des financements supplémentaires, mais pour bénéficier de la technicité, de l’expertise et des instruments qui nous permettent de mieux piloter notre économie », a insisté Amadou Oury Bah. Tout en présentant cette approbation comme un « grand pas » pour le pays, le Premier ministre reconnaît que le plus grand défi reste désormais celui de la mise en œuvre. Au cours des trois prochaines années, l’administration guinéenne devra renforcer ses capacités opérationnelles et améliorer ses performances dans la gestion des ressources publiques afin de respecter les engagements pris dans le cadre de ce programme et de répondre aux attentes sociales des populations

items.title: Haruna backs GTEC’s nationwide audit of PhD programmes
items.description: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has thrown his weight behind the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission’s (GTEC) nationwide assessment of PhD programmes, insisting that the exercise is necessary to safeguard academic standards and the credibility of doctoral qualifications awarded in the country. He said Ghana’s priority should be to produce well-trained doctoral graduates rather than expand enrolment without ensuring that universities have the capacity to deliver quality training. Mr Iddrisu made the remarks at the 2026 National Education Week and Evidence Summit in Accra on Monday, November 23, amid public criticism of GTEC Director-General, Professor Ahmed Abdulai Jinapor, over the audit and the suspension of new admissions to PhD programmes. He explained that the assessment would provide a clearer picture of institutions running doctoral programmes, the disciplines they cover, the number of candidates they admit and the adequacy of their academic resources. It would also help determine whether doctoral training in the country was producing the expertise needed to advance national development. The Minister said concerns had been raised about some universities admitting large numbers of PhD candidates without sufficient qualified supervisors and the necessary resources to provide effective academic guidance. He argued that such gaps could undermine the standard of research and the value of doctoral qualifications. “I see he’s also come under some public criticism heavily with his audit of PhDs. What we need as a country is not quantity, but quality. To undertake an audit is only to appreciate who is being trained, where they are being trained, in which area are being trained, and how is that consistent with our national development objectives?” he said. Mr Iddrisu further sought to allay concerns that the restrictions on new admissions amounted to an indefinite closure of doctoral programmes. He said the current measures were linked to the assessment and should not be interpreted as a permanent ban on PhD admissions. “It is not a ban into perpetuity. I’m sure when the audit is over, they will do what is needful and appreciate that,” he added. The audit is part of GTEC’s broader quality assurance efforts to examine the capacity of tertiary institutions to run doctoral programmes and ensure that candidates receive the supervision and academic support required for advanced research. The outcome is expected to inform decisions on the future operation and admission arrangements of PhD programmes across the country.

items.title: Amputee Football: Kofi Adams pledges $10K bonus for each Black Challenge player after World Cup triumph
items.description: Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams has pledged an additional US$10,000 bonus for each player on Ghana’s Black Challenge squad after their triumph at the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup. Ghana defeated Morocco 1-0 in Sunday’s final to lift the trophy and become world champions, with a second-half own goal proving decisive. As part of efforts to celebrate the team’s achievement, the Sports Minister sent a delegation to the team’s hotel in Mexico, comprising the Ministry’s Sports Protocol Officer, Dinah Boateng, and Chief Director, Fati Lily Soale, to engage with the players. Adams joined the meeting virtually via Zoom to congratulate the team on their historic achievement before announcing the additional financial package. “Aside from all the bonuses and other monies that have been paid to the team, we as a ministry are also adding an extra US$10,000 for each player of the team,” he said. The Black Challenge are expected to arrive in Ghana on Thursday at 1:00 pm, with their return scheduled at the Kotoka International Airport following their historic World Cup success in Mexico.

Cette rencontre amicale a offert au public un spectacle engagé, a encore commenté l'Ambassade de Suisse, qui a tenu à rappeler qu'au-delà de l'enjeu sportif, ce test-match revêtait une dimension symbolique particulière puisqu'il était organisé en hommage à feu Imed Noomani. L »événement a été organisé par la Fédération Tunisienne de Rugby (FTR), en étroite collaboration avec l'Association des Anciens Internationaux de Rugby (AAIR). Une initiative qui a permis de célébrer, sur le terrain comme en dehors, les valeurs fondamentales de solidarité, d'engagement et de transmission qui animent le rugby, souligne encore la même source. items.title: Guerre de leadership entre Alpha Amadou et Boubacar Biro à la Féguiboxe : du ring de la boxe au box des accusés
items.description: Le procès opposant les acteurs de la Fédération guinéenne de boxe (Feguiboxe) s’est poursuivi ce lundi 23 novembre 2026 devant le tribunal de première instance (TPI) de Kaloum. À l’audience, trois témoins ont été entendus à titre de renseignement avant la comparution de Boubacar Biro Barry, qui a catégoriquement rejeté les accusations portées contre lui. Parmi les témoins entendus figurait Amadou Tanta Diallo, entraîneur de boxe et ancien directeur technique national en 2022. Dans sa déposition, ce connaisseur de la discipline a retracé les différentes péripéties liées à la gestion de la fédération, ainsi que les épisodes de la crise qui secoue cette instance sportive. À sa suite, Tallatou Garanké Diallo et Alpha Amadou Barry ont également livré leurs témoignages. Tous deux ont notamment évoqué les répercussions de cette crise sur les boxeurs guinéens, particulièrement sur la scène internationale. Ils ont par ailleurs affirmé ne pas connaître le bureau présidé par Boubacar Biro Barry, installé en mai 2026. Appelé à la barre, ce dernier a contesté l’ensemble des faits mis à sa charge. Il a notamment dénoncé les dysfonctionnements qui, selon lui, ont longtemps caractérisé la gestion de la fédération. « L’historique de la Fédération guinéenne de boxe est un désordre qui ne dit pas son nom. Notre mission en 2022 était de régulariser ce désordre », a-t-il déclaré. Poursuivi pour « usurpation de titre et de fonction » et « faux en écriture », Boubacar Biro Barry, ancien secrétaire général de la fédération au sein du bureau de 2022, a également estimé que ce différend n'aurait jamais dû être porté devant la justice. À l’en croire, à la veille du 2 octobre dernier, le secrétaire général du ministère des Sports, Billy Kaba, aurait invité les protagonistes à privilégier un règlement de la crise au sein du département. Une démarche qui n’aurait toutefois pas reçu l’adhésion du président de la fédération, Alpha Amadou Baldé, à l'origine de la procédure judiciaire. Face aux accusations de falsification et d’usurpation, le prévenu s'est montré catégorique dans sa défense : « moi, je n’ai falsifié l’écriture de personne, je n’ai usurpé le titre de personne et je n’ai modifié la signature de personne. » À l’issue des débats, le tribunal a renvoyé l’affaire au 30 novembre 2026 pour les réquisitions et les plaidoiries.

items.title: 11 Décembre 2026 : Le Burkina renoue avec les grandes célébrations et annonce une parade militaire d'envergure inédite
items.description: La célébration du 66ᵉ anniversaire de l'indépendance du Burkina Faso aura lieu sous le thème : « Révolution progressiste populaire au Burkina Faso : une consécration des résiliences à la domination coloniale et à l'impérialisme ». Le programme des activités a été dévoilé ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, au cours d'une conférence de presse animée par le président du comité national d'organisation, le général de brigade Théophile Nikièma. Après cinq années d'arrêt, le Burkina Faso célébrera cette année le 11 décembre. Pour l'édition 2026, les autorités entendent marquer l'événement à travers trois grandes activités. Il y aura une cérémonie officielle ponctuée par une parade militaire et paramilitaire, des conférences publiques et des projections populaires de films. Le moment phare de cette célébration sera la grande parade militaire et paramilitaire prévue le vendredi 11 décembre 2026, à partir de 9 heures, sur l'avenue Pascal-Zagré, à Ouaga 2000. Selon le président du comité national d'organisation, le général de brigade Théophile Nikièma, cette parade sera d'une envergure inédite. « C'est une grande parade militaire et paramilitaire d'envergure inédite et jamais réalisée par nos troupes, aussi bien en termes d'effectifs qu'en moyens logistiques », a-t-il annoncé. À Ouagadougou, le défilé motorisé connaîtra également la participation des structures et entités issues des Initiatives présidentielles, afin de mettre en lumière le volet développement. Dans les autres chefs-lieux de régions, la cérémonie officielle sera essentiellement marquée par un défilé militaire et paramilitaire. Le président du comité national d'organisation, le général de brigade Théophile Nikièma La conférence inaugurale est prévue le 2 décembre 2026 dans la salle des Conférences internationales de Ouaga 2000. Elle sera suivie de conférences régionales qui se tiendront du 2 au 7 décembre sur l'ensemble du territoire national. Autre activité majeure annoncée : les projections populaires de films consacrés à la défense du territoire national et aux résistances à la domination coloniale. Ces projections se dérouleront dans différents espaces publics, notamment les places publiques, les salles de cinéma et les garnisons. Parmi les œuvres annoncées figure le documentaire de reconstitution historique « Kidiga », ainsi que d'autres productions inédites actuellement en cours de réalisation. En plus de ces trois principales activités, plusieurs manifestations connexes viendront enrichir le programme. Le mardi 8 décembre 2026, Ouagadougou accueillera un cross populaire suivi d'un méga aérobic. Le 10 décembre sera notamment consacré à des actions sociales. Une campagne de consultations médicales gratuites et une opération de délivrance de cartes nationales d'identité AES seront organisées dans toutes les régions du pays. La même journée connaîtra également la cérémonie de clôture du Tournoi de la relance de l'Office de liaison de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (OLAO), à Ouagadougou. L'édition 2026 sera aussi marquée par un changement d'identité visuelle. Un nouveau logotype et une nouvelle charte graphique accompagneront désormais la célébration nationale. Selon le président du comité national d'organisation, cette nouvelle identité traduit « la fierté retrouvée d'un peuple qui assume son histoire et exerce sa souveraineté ». Le logotype de la célébration À travers cette programmation, les autorités souhaitent donner une dimension particulière à la célébration de l'indépendance, en mettant en avant les valeurs de souveraineté, de résistance et de développement. Le général de brigade Théophile Nikièma a, pour terminer, invité les Burkinabè de l'intérieur comme ceux de la diaspora à prendre part aux différentes activités dans l'ordre et la discipline. Il a également sollicité l'accompagnement des médias pour assurer une couverture rigoureuse et professionnelle de cet événement national. Rama Diallo Lefaso.net

items.title: US experts join Ghana’s fight against mercury pollution in rivers
items.description: A team of United States scientists visited Ghana to support efforts to tackle mercury pollution linked to illegal small-scale gold mining and strengthen freshwater protection. The delegation visited from November 7 to 21, bringing together specialists from the US Department of the Interior, the US Geological Survey (USGS) and the US Environmental Protection Agency. Their work focused on water quality monitoring, mercury detection, laboratory capacity and sustainable mining practices. The visit took place under the Ambassador’s Water Experts Program, a joint initiative of the US Departments of State and the Interior. During consultations with Ghana’s Environmental Protection Agency, the experts discussed mercury contamination in freshwater systems affected by galamsey. They also examined the need for standardised testing methods and closer scientific collaboration. The engagement builds on a 2024 baseline assessment by USGS scientist and former Embassy Science Fellow Dr Grace Armstrong. Her research identified elevated mercury levels in the waters and sediments of the Pra and Ankobra river systems. Dr Armstrong returned to Ghana as part of the latest visit. “The challenges posed by mercury pollution require coordinated scientific approaches and trusted partnerships,” she said. “Our work together helps ensure that data collected in Ghana meets rigorous standards and supports effective decision-making for environmental protection.” A two-day symposium on November 10 and 11 brought together US and Ghanaian experts, civil society organisations, academics and industry representatives. Held under the theme, “Addressing Mercury Pollution: Collaborative Solutions for Sustainable Mining in Ghana,” it examined the environmental, health and security effects of mercury use. Participants also explored practical and commercially viable mercury-free mining technologies. Speaking at the symposium, then US Chargé d’Affaires Rolf Olson said protecting freshwater resources was critical to Ghana’s future. “Protecting Ghana’s freshwater resources is essential not only for environmental and public health, but also for long-term economic and food security,” he said. “The United States is committed to working with Ghana to strengthen scientific capacity, advance responsible mining practices, and promote American technological solutions that support sustainable development.” US Environmental Protection Agency expert Dr Chris Eckley also highlighted the potential value of sharing technical experience. “Drawing on U.S. experience assessing and remediating mercury-contaminated sites could help our Ghanaian counterparts address local environmental challenges,” he said. The delegation engaged students, researchers, civil society organisations and youth groups on water protection, training and field research. Participating institutions included the University of Ghana, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, the University of Environment and Sustainable Development, and Accra STEM Academy. The exchanges aimed to improve the reliability of laboratory analyses and support the adoption of international best practices in water-quality monitoring and mercury detection.

items.title: Finance inclusive : L’IFIC – SA tient sa première rencontre avec ses actionnaires à Ouagadougou
items.description: Les actionnaires de la nouvelle société Initiative Finance Inclusive et Crédit (IFIC – SA) se sont réunis ce samedi 21 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. L’objectif de cette rencontre était d’échanger sur le lancement de cette nouvelle structure et d’examiner ses textes fondateurs. Cette étape concrétise la mise en conformité réglementaire de l’association initiatrice tout en posant des bases solides pour son développement futur. Depuis plusieurs années, la réglementation impose aux associations exerçant une activité de microfinance de se transformer en société coopérative ou en société anonyme. C’est dans cette optique que l’Association pour la Promotion de la Finance Inclusive (APEFI) a sollicité des personnes physiques et morales afin de répondre favorablement à cette injonction de l’État. Une fois la nouvelle entité constituée, ses dirigeants ont souhaité réunir les actionnaires pour favoriser les échanges et leur permettre de s’approprier les textes. Selon Hamadou Bonkoungou, président du conseil d’administration de l’IFIC, cette mobilisation a permis d’aboutir à la création de la société anonyme, bien que l’association APEFI continue d’exister en parallèle. Pour lui, cette journée a surtout permis de réunir la dizaine d’actionnaires qui ont fait confiance au projet. « L’objet de la réunion de ce matin était de permettre aux différents actionnaires et acteurs de l’IFIC de faire connaissance, suite à la transformation juridique de l’APEFI en société anonyme. Il s’agissait également de parcourir l’ensemble des textes qui régissent la vie de cette nouvelle société », a-t-il expliqué. Cette mutation répond aux exigences de la loi n°001-2025/ALT du 13 février 2025 portant réglementation de la microfinance au Burkina Faso, qui impose ce changement de statut juridique aux institutions associatives. « La prochaine étape consiste à lancer les activités. Comme vous le savez, l’ancienne structure connaissait certaines difficultés. Il fallait donc prendre les mesures nécessaires pour relancer nos opérations à travers cette nouvelle entité », a-t-il ajouté. Pour rappel, Initiative Finance Inclusive & Crédit (IFIC – SA) est une société anonyme avec conseil d’administration dotée d’un capital de 200 000 000FCFA. Issue de la transformation de l’APEFI conformément à la loi de février 2025, elle a pour ambition d’offrir aux ménages, aux petits producteurs, aux commerçants ainsi qu’aux micro et petites entreprises des services d’épargne, de crédit et de paiement adaptés à leurs besoins. items.title: National Security summons Suame artisans over attacks on foreign traders
items.description: National Security has stepped in to address growing tensions at the Suame Industrial Enclave in Kumasi, inviting some local artisans for a meeting on Tuesday, November 24, following attacks on foreign spare-parts dealers. The engagement is expected to give the aggrieved artisans an opportunity to formally present their complaints about the business practices of foreign traders, particularly Nigerians, whom they accuse of undercutting Ghanaian-owned businesses through what they describe as unfair pricing. The invitation comes after a protest by some artisans, who wore red armbands and demonstrated against the increasing presence of foreign operators in the spare-parts trade. However, the demonstration descended into violence, with some protesters attacking individuals believed to be foreign traders. Videos circulating from the incident showed one man being grabbed by the neck and kicked to the ground by members of the group. The protesters also shut down at least 10 shops belonging to foreign dealers and pasted notices on their entrances as they sought to draw attention to their grievances. The artisans contend that some foreign traders are able to sell spare parts at prices that local businesses cannot match, putting Ghanaian operators under pressure and threatening their livelihoods. Police and National Security personnel intervened following the disturbances and restored calm at the enclave. Tuesday’s meeting is expected to provide a platform for the artisans to explain their concerns and enable the authorities to consider steps towards resolving the dispute. The engagement comes amid the need to address the traders’ complaints without allowing commercial disagreements to degenerate into intimidation, violence or attacks on individuals and businesses.National Security has stepped in to address growing tensions at the Suame Industrial Enclave in Kumasi, inviting some local artisans for a meeting on Tuesday, November 24, following attacks on foreign spare-parts dealers. items.title: Inauguration de l’Académie technologique du Faso : « Que chaque apprenant et chaque enseignant soit marqué du sceau de l’excellence », dit le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 23 novembre 2026). Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, a procédé à l’inauguration officielle, ce lundi matin, de l’Académie Technologique du Faso (ATF). Onze mois après le lancement des travaux, l’achèvement de ce chantier d’envergure consacre la détermination et l’ambition du Burkina Faso à maîtriser les sciences pour façonner son avenir. La coupure du ruban par le Chef de l'État a ouvert les portes d’un complexe moderne, pensé pour conjuguer rigueur académique et pratique. Au fil de la visite guidée, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a d’abord parcouru le bloc administratif, cœur de pilotage de ce temple de savoir, avant de découvrir les ateliers de fabrication et d’électronique, où les premiers étudiants s'adonnent déjà à des manipulations techniques. La visite s’est poursuivie dans les autres entités notamment le réfectoire et les logements, des infrastructures indispensables pour offrir aux pensionnaires un cadre de vie digne et propice à la concentration et à l’excellence. « Vous aurez la pression, vous aurez toutes sortes de pressions » Au terme du parcours, un échange avec la communauté éducative a permis au Président du Faso de rappeler les responsabilités qui incombent à chacun : « Je souhaite que chaque apprenant et chaque enseignant qui séjourne ici soit marqué du sceau de l’excellence et en porte l’étendard dans sa vie active », a-t-il déclaré. Pour le Capitaine TRAORÉ, « un peuple qui n’est pas audacieux ne développe pas sa science et ne la fait pas avancer ». Il a invité les étudiants à oser, conformément à la devise de l’ATF : Génie – Audace – Discipline. « Il n’y a pas de magie : le travail scientifique, et le travail tout court, demande de la discipline », a insisté le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, qui a appelé les nouveaux étudiants à ne se donner aucune limite dans le sens de la créativité. Une immense joie pour les tout-premiers étudiants La porte-parole des étudiants de cette première cuvée, la Camarade Yéri Cynthia Djamila KAMBOU, dit avoir versé des larmes de joie à son arrivée à l’ATF : des rêves d’études à l’étranger qui s’effacent soudainement face à une réalité jugée autrefois inaccessible au Burkina Faso. Elle a adressé ses vifs remerciements au Chef de l'État pour avoir cru en la jeunesse burkinabè à travers la réalisation de cette académie et a réaffirmé son engagement et celui de ses camarades autour du triptyque « Génie, audace, discipline ». Pour sa part, le Directeur exécutif du Bureau National des Grands Projets du Burkina (BN-GPB), Pr Hamidou SAWADOGO, a précisé que l’ATF a été bâtie en exactement dix mois et dix-huit jours, grâce à la mobilisation d’une main-d’œuvre nationale et sur fonds propres. L’ATF, comme l’a inscrit le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ dans le livre d’or, incarne le choix souverain d’investir dans l’intelligence et de libérer le génie créateur de la jeunesse. Elle s’érige désormais en symbole d’audace collective au service du progrès national durable. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: Nvidia value climbs by almost $1tn and tech stocks rally after Jensen Huang returns
items.description: Nvidia’s market value rose by nearly $1 trillion as its share price skyrocketed after the tech firm reinstated Jensen Huang as its chief executive with immediate effect. His shock reinstatement comes less than two weeks after Huang resigned after admitting an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy, a period in which shares in the chipmaker have also fallen significantly. Nvidia shares rose more than 31%, lifting stock markets, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq up 6.5% and the S&P 500 up 4.75%. Tech stocks have also rallied after large falls on Friday , with much of the rally starting in pre-market trading before Huang’s return was announced. Other chipmakers experienced large increases following Monday’s announcement from the Nvidia board. Micron Technology shares jumped 19%, while AMD shares rose nearly 7%. Tesla shares also lept up by nearly 11.5%, while other tech gains were more muted by comparison: Amazon shares were up nearly 3.5%, and Apple and Microsoft rose by less than 2%. While the surge in Nvidia shares was large and drove its market value back towards $4tn,the firm’s share price remains about 21% down from a month ago. A sharp drop occurred on 4 November, after the Democrat’s midterm election victory sparked fears of tougher AI regulation to come led to a broad tech stock sell-off. On Friday alone, Nvidia shares fell by 13.7% as tech stocks more broadly fell, and as Reuters reported – unconfirmed by the BBC – that the company was being investigated by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) over its accounting practices. Nvidia is a key firm at the core of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, with its chips central to the industry. Nvidia’s board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate the firm’s co-founder following “a series of discussions and meetings” with him, the company said – but US President Donald Trump has claimed he “convinced” the board to reinstate Huang. Kathleen Brooks, research director at brokerage firm XTB, said Huang’s return showed Huang was the “godfather” of AI, and “has a talismanic influence over the sector”. “Barely two weeks ago this man was ousted from the company that he founded due to serious misconduct and potential national security issues,” she said. “Even though Huang did not hold special voting shares on the board, Nvidia’s directors cannot see a future for the company without him.” Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said Huang’s reinstatement was an astonishing about-turn for Nvidia, particularly given reports of an as-yet unconfirmed SEC investigation. “This is the biggest corporate U-turn in living memory. To go from being embroiled in a spy scandal to being reinstated as the head of one of the world’s most valuable companies in less than a fortnight is nothing short of remarkable,” he said. “Today’s stock market rebound represents a massive sigh of relief for investors. However, Huang cannot rule out a more conservative approach going forward. “His every move will be scrutinised by the market, and he may wish to tread more carefully to protect his integrity and ensure that Nvidia is being run responsibly.” Politicians are also demanding greater scrutiny. Senator Jeanne Shaheen, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, said Huang’s reinstatement “reportedly at the encouragement of Trump Administration officials and without any apparent accounting or response to the risks to our national security, demands an explanation.” She added: “What is abundantly clear is that the AI industry requires guardrails and oversight.”

items.title: Court restrains CLOGSAG’s 15th Quadrennial National Congress
items.description: The High Court in Accra has granted an interim injunction restraining the Civil and Local Government Staff Association of Ghana (CLOGSAG) from holding its 15th Quadrennial National Congress scheduled for November 23 to 25, 2026. The Congress was expected to take place at the Pentecost Convention Centre at Gomoa Fetteh near Kasoa. According to a statement from the Office of the Acting President of CLOGSAG, the injunction, granted on November 19, 2026, remains in force pending the Court’s determination of the matter. The statement urged all persons and institutions involved in planning, organising, facilitating, or conducting the Congress to fully comply with the court order and refrain from any activities prohibited under the injunction. It said the court’s decision was intended to preserve the status quo while the judicial process resolved leadership and governance issues within the Association. The statement further appealed to members to remain calm, exercise restraint and avoid any actions that could undermine the legal proceedings or create tension within the Association. Members were also cautioned against taking the law into their own hands. Mr Benjamin Arkaah Otoo, Acting President of CLOGSAG, called on members to remain united, vigilant and committed to the rule of law while the case remained before the Court. The statement said the Association would share further information on the matter through its official channels.

items.title: Angustia de 680 alumnos y los padres del histórico colegio Decroly, que abandona el concierto en Madrid
items.description: Los dueños del histórico Decroly, el único colegio laico concertado del barrio de Chamberí , han renunciado a renovar la concesión con la Comunidad de Madrid, según ha confirmado EL PAÍS con fuentes oficiales. Las familias de los más de 600 niños matriculados en la institución se encuentran en shock y angustiadas por esta medida, que les ha tomado por sorpresa. items.title: 2027: NUC proposes 4-week break for universities
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks. Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, made the proposal on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN. According to a statement from INEC on Monday night, Amupitan was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior officials of the commission. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027. He noted that the academic community had for over a decade served as the backbone of collation and declaration of results, with Vice-Chancellors serving as Collation and Returning Officers across the Federation. The INEC Chairman said the commission had introduced operational, technological and security reforms to make the work of its university partners safer and less contentious. He said polling unit results on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). According to him, the commission has procured 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and lowered the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine. Amupitan added that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Saturday, 28 November 2026. On security, he said the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to every Local Government Area and Registration Area, with dedicated security cordons and escort protocols around collation centres. He drew attention to Sections 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalise violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, and Section 148, which empowers the commission to prosecute offenders directly. “No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” Amupitan said. He then asked the NUC for support in four areas: the timely nomination of academic staff of verified non-partisan standing, the alignment of academic calendars with the election dates, collaboration on voter education and counter-disinformation on campuses, and the welfare and recognition of academics deployed for election duty. Responding, Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute and “a round peg in a round hole.” , The NUC Executive Secretary said the commission would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of academic staff, including through an online meeting. He said it would also transmit a circular to the universities once INEC forwards a formal letter on the matter. “Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel,” Ribadu said. He added that all ad hoc personnel should take an oath of neutrality. On the academic calendar, he said the entire election cycle would last no more than four weeks, and suggested that universities could adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate it. “We will discuss with the Vice-Chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” Ribadu said. He said students could also support voter education through campus clubs. Ribadu expressed confidence that INEC would deliver a transparent, free and fair election that would serve as an example to other African countries. He proposed expanded collaboration between the two institutions, including student internships at INEC offices, a possible programme in electoral studies, and joint research on artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics. SAITO, Ambassadeur du Japon en Tunisie. Co-inventeur de la « Méthode de Fukuoka » une technique de décharge semi-aérobie qui réduit les émissions de gaz à effet de serre et améliore la santé publique, le Prof. MATSUFUJI a conduit avec son équipe une étude de faisabilité sur le terrain en vue d’introduire cette méthode à Sejnane. Ils se sont appuyés sur l’expérience pilote déjà réalisée à la décharge de Béja. Merci au Gouvernement du Japon pour son engagement constant en faveur d’un développement urbain durable en Tunisie, et à la Municipalité de Sejnane pour sa mobilisation. items.title: Presidency orders state CEOs who have reached retirement limits to vacate office
items.description: Chief Executives of public institutions and state-owned organisations who have exceeded the constitutional retirement limits have been directed to hand over and vacate office, following a new instruction from the Office of the President. The directive requires all Ministers of State to ensure that CEOs under their respective oversight comply with Article 199 of the 1992 Constitution, which sets the compulsory retirement age for public officers at 60, subject to specified exceptions and re-engagement arrangements. In a letter dated November 23, 2026, and signed by the Secretary to the President, Dr Callistus Mahama, ministers were instructed to ensure that affected chief executives submit their handing-over notes to their respective Boards or Councils without delay. The instruction applies to CEOs who have attained the age of 60 but are serving without a valid post-retirement contract, as well as those whose contracts have expired or who have exhausted the maximum period permitted for re-engagement. The Presidency cited Article 199(4), which allows an appointing authority to re-engage a retired public officer where the needs of the service require it. Under the provision, such engagements may be granted for periods of up to two years at a time, but must not exceed five years cumulatively. The letter explained that where re-engagement begins at age 60, the maximum period would end at age 65. It therefore directed that chief executives who have reached the applicable limits should complete the handover process and leave office. Those approaching the end of their lawful tenure must submit their handing-over notes by their final day in office. The handing-over notes are expected to outline ongoing programmes, outstanding decisions and commitments, and issues requiring the immediate attention of the relevant Board or Council. The directive places responsibility on ministers to ensure that institutions under their supervision comply with the constitutional requirements.

items.title: Ghana Bauxite Company commits to opening Awaso to commercial activity
items.description: The Ghana Bauxite Company Limited says it is deliberately using its expanding operations at Awaso to open the catchment communities to wider commercial activity. After the mine’s takeover by the IOP Group, investments are being made to improve its operations and expand job opportunities. According to the General Manager, Alexander Gyedu, the group targets enhancing the local economies of the mine’s catchment area through industrialisation. “It is the story of how an established industrial operation can become a catalyst around which other businesses, services, skills, and investments begin to grow,” he said. Mr. Gyedu emphasised: “When an enterprise grows, the true measure of its impact is not only what happens inside its gates. It is what begins to happen around those gates.” He was speaking at the opening of the Ecobank Awaso Branch, which comes after the signing of a $250-million funding agreement with Ecobank Ghana to finance the company’s expansion drive. GBC has in recent years been investing in mining operations, equipment, logistics, and operating capability, moving away from traditional drill-and-blast methods towards more modern mining techniques. That expansion is also connected to Ghana’s National Integrated Aluminium Industry Programme, which identifies the expansion of the Awaso mine and the development of an alumina refinery as critical to the country’s aluminium industry strategy. GBC argued the growth being realised is expected to drive local economies in the catchment communities. The company’s partnership with Ecobank has resulted in the opening of the bank’s new branch at Awaso, which is expected to improve banking services for residents. Speaking at the opening of the new branch, the Executive Director of Corporate and Investment Banking for Ghana and Anglophone West Africa for Ecobank, Henry Ampong, revealed the bank’s decision to establish a presence in the community was part of a broader commitment to making banking services accessible to people in emerging economies. He emphasised commitment to supporting small and medium-sized enterprises, and to advancing women-led and women-owned businesses. Meanwhile, Western North Regional Minister, Wilbert Petty Brentum, also linked the bank’s opening to Awaso’s strategic location and the government’s infrastructure agenda for the Western North Region. He said many roads in the region are receiving a facelift to enhance business. He also said discussions are ongoing to bring back the railway from Awaso to Takoradi, and pointed to interest expressed at a recent investment summit in Accra in supporting railway infrastructure and in putting up a bigger agricultural warehouse in Awaso, from which farm produce from the hinterlands could be brought to Awaso and transported by rail to Takoradi and other places. “Setting up a bank here in Awaso is very strategic,” the Regional Minister said, urging residents to open accounts with Ecobank to make its presence in Awaso sustainable and to encourage expansion to other areas. The relationship between the two institutions goes beyond the branch. On 28th October 2026, GBC appointed Ecobank Ghana as exclusive mandated arranger for proposed financing facilities of up to US$250,000,000 to support the next phase of GBC’s mine expansion, including capital investment and working capital requirements. GBC stressed that the branch opening and the financing transaction are distinct matters, but said together they demonstrate how economic ecosystems develop. “Investment attracts services. Services enable enterprise. Enterprise creates opportunity. And opportunity, when it is responsibly managed, becomes development,” Mr. Gyedu said. That multiplier effect, GBC said, is what it wants to see around the mine – local entrepreneurs graduating from small informal transactions into properly managed enterprises, and young people seeing that an industrial economy creates careers, not only for miners, but for accountants, bankers, technicians, engineers, geologists, IT specialists, environmental specialists, and business owners. GBC has established a dedicated Community Relations Office in Awaso to create a more structured channel for engaging surrounding communities, including local enterprises, initiatives, and community programmes.

items.title: US Exchange Alumni Summit: Past fellow struggle to access post-fellowship grants, limiting knowledge-transfer applications
items.description: A 2019 Mandela Washington Fellow, Dr Joel Afi Duah, says it is becoming increasingly difficult for beneficiaries of development programs in the United States of America to access post-fellowship grants following donor cuts in the US. Dr. Duah, who is the municipal director of Health Services for Tano South in the Ahafo Region, says the situation has limited alumni efforts to translate knowledge and skills acquired through exchange programmes into practical development projects. He was speaking at the U.S. Embassy Ghana Exchange Alumni Summit in Kumasi. “With the cuts in funding, alumni are leveraging their networks and available resources to sustain their work. However, it has become quite difficult to plan and execute capital projects and meet other major expenses,” he said. He called on the government to increase funding for public institutions struggling with reductions and withdrawals in support from international development partners. He says funding cuts by organisations, including the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and the United States African Development Foundation (USADF), have disrupted development programmes and weakened the capacity of institutions and beneficiaries to sustain ongoing initiatives. “We are therefore making a passionate appeal to the government to step up funding support in areas where donor funding has been reduced or withdrawn. This will enable us to build on the investments made and the knowledge and skills we have acquired through these fellowship programmes,” he asserted. Dr Duah believes increased government investment will be critical to sustaining the gains made through international partnerships and ensuring that development initiatives do not stall because of funding constraints. The appeal comes as the U.S. Embassy in Ghana brings together about 100 alumni of U.S. government exchange programmes from the Ashanti Region and Ghana’s middle belt for an Alumni Excellence Summit in Kumasi. The event, held on Saturday, November 21, 2026, celebrated the contributions of former exchange programme participants to national development across various sectors. It also forms part of activities marking the 250th anniversary of American independence under the Freedom 250 initiative. Cultural Affairs Attaché at the U.S. Embassy in Ghana, Donya Eldridge, said the exchange programmes are intended to promote knowledge-sharing and expose participants to approaches the US has adopted in addressing development challenges that Ghana also faces. “Our alumni include students and professionals who have had the opportunity to learn from experiences in the United States. The idea is to share what they have done, the lessons they have learned, and help us understand how similar approaches can work in the Ghanaian economy,” she stated.

items.title: Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return amid US lawmakers’ spy allegations, security concerns
items.description: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk. Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag. The image appeared to allude to the scandal that forced Huang, co-founder of the AI chip giant, to resign less than two weeks earlier following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. “The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk. In a telephone interview with CNBC, Trump suggested the scandal could prove to be “a net positive” by highlighting Nvidia’s technological advances. “I don’t think he’s going to be diminished at all,” he said, predicting Huang would return at “an almost higher level.” He said the attorney general had confirmed that US authorities possessed no evidence Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct, but urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with restrictions on advanced chip sales to China. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries vowed sweeping investigations into Nvidia, Trump and his senior officials, with Jeffries singling out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. “We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump administration for personal financial gain,” Jeffries said. – ‘What changed?’ – Huang is already scheduled to face questioning behind closed doors by three House committees on December 1 over his relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative and concerns about Nvidia’s chip exports. And the Republican-led Senate Banking Committee has announced that his appearance scheduled for December 3 will be livestreamed. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him,” said House Intelligence Committee Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi, demanding a full public congressional hearing. Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and demanded details of what input senior administration officials had provided in support of Huang’s return. Republican Senator John Curtis raised similar questions, noting that Nvidia’s board had reversed its opposition to reinstating Huang while an independent investigation remained unfinished. “Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board?” he wrote on X. “I’d like to know what changed.” Senator Pete Ricketts, also a Republican, said Huang’s behavior did not warrant reinstatement and insisted the move did not excuse him from testifying before Congress. Former Republican House speaker Newt Gingrich called for scrutiny of what he described as a national security issue “of enormous proportions.” Outgoing Republican congressman Don Bacon alleged Huang had been “compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy,” demanding answers about who had authorized advanced chip sales to China. And Republican Senator John Cornyn offered a terse response to Trump’s assurances. “No national security risk? Based on what?” he wrote on X. Trump declined earlier Monday to comment on a New York Times report that the woman at the center of the scandal had been in contact with an official from China’s principal intelligence agency during her affair with Huang.
