items.title: Nigeria’s rice revolution collapses as 90 mills shutdown
items.description: *Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) and Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos) Nigeria’s much-celebrated rice revolution is facing a major reversal, with more than 90 out of the country’s 260 integrated rice mills shutting down completely over acute paddy scarcity, rising production costs and the influx of cheaper imported rice. This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026. The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021. But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent. Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity. Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023. The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years. More recently they said that 2026 has witnessed a deliberate opening of the country’s borders allowing massive importation of cheaper foreign rice especially through Seme border with Benin Republic. They lamented that Nigerians have invested heavily in building rice mills but the government has failed to sustain the agricultural production policy needed to keep them running. Paradox of idle capacity, imports Perhaps the most disturbing aspect of the current crisis is the contradiction between Nigeria’s enormous milling capacity and the shortage of locally produced paddy. According to Dama, the country has installed rice milling capacity of approximately 7.5 million tonnes annually but currently produces only 4.1 million tonnes of paddy. This leaves a huge gap between the capacity of the industry and the raw materials available to sustain its operations. The operators noted cost over-run as the main factor stoking the crises as a tonne of paddy that sold for about N180,000 in 2021 now costs between N600,000 and N650,000. Fertiliser prices, according to them, have increased from about N8,000 to N45,000, while petrol has risen from N250 to N1,400 per litre. The input cost, according to them, has made the local rice now uncompetitive against the imported brands. Dama said, ‘‘locally milled rice at current paddy prices costs higher than imported finished rice through Lagos ports. ‘‘This is a fundamental competitiveness problem that cannot be resolved merely by announcing restrictions on rice imports’’. Consequently, some farmers are abandoning rice for alternative crops such as sesame and sorghum, further worsening the shortage of paddy. The crises, according to the operators, goes beyond the fortunes of rice mill owners to include farmers, transporters, distributors, workers and millions of households that depend on rice as a staple food. Why rice value chain now struggling — FG A top official of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said that the main challenge facing the rice value chain is policy inconsistency. He said three other factors combined to create the current gap in rice production and the consumption needs of the Nigerian society. According to him the growing population, rural-urban migration and the changing eating pattern of Nigerians combined to put pressure on rice, which is a staple food in almost every part of the country. He said Nigeria remains the largest producer but also the largest importer of rice due to the inability of production to meet demand. He revealed that the nation’s current self-sufficiency in rice production has dropped to 69 percent. He however lamented that the cost of inputs such as fertilisers, seeds and agro-chemicals have challenged farmers lately, especially since the end of the Presidential Fertiliser Initiative (PFI) initiative when Urea was imported from Morocco and sold to fertilizer blenders at subsidized rate, who in turn sold fertilisers to farmers at subsidised rates. According to him, fertiliser blenders now buy urea at market prices and that combined with the geopolitical crisis in the Middle East, especially the blockade of the Strait of Homuz, where 30 percent of fertiliser raw material pass, the fertiliser market has become more challenged, making the products more expensive and out of reach for many small-holder farmers. He added that with very expensive inputs, paddy produced is sold to millers at high prices. He confessed that millers who also face high operational costs due largely to dependence on diesel, rather than electricity come up with milled rice that cannot compete with the imported rice. According to him, governments of the countries of origin of imported rice subsidise rice production for export and that as such, locally milled rice is struggling to compete with the imported rice. He suggested that if rice production is to significantly increase in the country, the government must consider a way of subsidizing agricultural inputs, as is the case with other countries of the world. Collapse of ABP At the heart of the crisis, according to the operators, is the collapse of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme, ABP, introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria under former Governor Godwin Emefiele. The programme was one of the most ambitious attempts to address Nigeria’s food import dependence by linking smallholder farmers with processors and providing them with affordable agricultural financing. Between 2015 and 2021, it reportedly helped increase paddy production from 2.5 million tonnes to 8.5 million tonnes. Official rice imports, according to figures supplied by industry stakeholders, fell from 2.4 million tonnes to less than 400,000 tonnes during the period. The programme’s strength was its integrated approach to agricultural production. Rather than simply giving farmers cash, it provided seeds, fertiliser and herbicides on credit, with repayment made in paddy after harvest. It also linked farmers to rice millers who guaranteed markets for their produce. Interest rates were pegged at nine per cent, significantly below the commercial lending rates of about 28 per cent cited by industry stakeholders. This arrangement addressed two major constraints confronting farmers: access to inputs and guaranteed markets. It also provided millers with a more predictable supply of paddy. However, the programme became controversial over allegations of politicisation, poor loan recovery and the inclusion of beneficiaries who were not genuine farmers. Although more than N1.1 trillion was reportedly disbursed, loan recovery was said to have fallen below 30 per cent. Consequently, a new CBN leadership discontinued the programme in 2023 without an effective replacement arrangement. That decision created a financing vacuum in the rice value chain. Dama estimates that more than 40 per cent of smallholder farmers who participated in the programme have since moved into other crops. The Ministry of Agriculture’s dry-season wheat and rice initiatives, according to him, have not been sufficient to reach the majority of genuine farmers, while the Bank of Agriculture lacks the resources to provide financing on the scale required. Dama further argued that ‘‘it is not necessarily that the ABP should be restored in its original form. Its weaknesses, particularly poor loan recovery and political interference, must be addressed. ‘‘But dismantling a programme without putting a functional alternative in place has exposed the industry to precisely the production challenges it was designed to overcome’’. Cotonou smuggling challenge Commenting on the influx of cheaper imported rice, which local millers say is undermining their ability to compete, Dama described the situation as an open secret, alleging that more than 2.5 million tonnes of foreign rice entered Nigeria through the Benin Republic’s Cotonou port and porous land borders so far in 2026. He claimed that imported rice sells for between N52,000 and N60,000 per 50kg bag, compared with N75,000 to N80,000 for locally produced rice. The price difference makes foreign rice attractive to consumers, particularly households struggling with the rising cost of living. More troubling, according to him, is his allegation that some lower quality imported rice is repackaged and sold as Nigerian rice in major markets across Lagos, Abuja, Kano and Ibadan. If the allegation is established, it points to a serious enforcement failure, with implications for consumer confidence, local investment and government revenue. The tariff differential between Nigeria and Benin Republic is also contributing to the problem. According to Dama, Nigeria imposes a 70 per cent duty, compared with 35 per cent in Benin, creating an incentive for traders to route rice imports through the neighbouring country. He therefore called for the implementation of the ECOWAS Rice Roadmap 2025-2035, which provides for a common external tariff of 35 per cent for paddy and 50 per cent for milled rice across the 15 member states. ‘‘A harmonised regional tariff, combined with technology-driven border surveillance, could reduce the incentive for smuggling’’, Dama said. Lagos Lake Rice disappears The disappearance of Lake Rice from Lagos markets offers another illustration of the difficulty of sustaining agricultural partnerships beyond their initial political appeal. In 2016, Lagos and Kebbi states entered into a Memorandum of Understanding to promote rice production in Kebbi and processing and distribution in Lagos. The arrangement was designed to transport paddy from Kebbi to Lagos, where it would be milled, packaged and sold to consumers. The initiative was intended to connect farmers in the North with a major consumer market in the South. But the arrangement eventually collapsed. Investigations by Vanguard indicated that personal interests undermined the original agreement. Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s Special Adviser on Agriculture and Food Systems, Dr Oluwarotimi Fashola, said the initiative was discontinued because the original understanding between the two states was not followed. According to him, the agreement was for Kebbi to supply paddy to Lagos for milling and packaging, rather than for finished rice supplied by a private consulting firm to be repackaged and distributed as Lake Rice. The industry stakeholders said the collapse of the arrangement underscores the importance of transparency, accountability and strict adherence to agreed terms in public-private agricultural partnerships. They also said it illustrates how potentially beneficial agricultural arrangements can fail when institutional interests and implementation shortcomings undermine their original objectives. Women farmers and the financing gap The consequences of the collapse of agricultural financing are also being felt by women farmers, particularly in Kebbi State. The Chairperson of Kebbi State Female Farmers Associations, Hajia Hadiza Kola, identified inadequate funding as a major obstacle to expanding agricultural production following the end of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme. She said women faced additional social challenges because farming was traditionally regarded in parts of the state as an occupation largely reserved for men. Some women also struggle to obtain the support of their husbands to participate in commercial farming. Nevertheless, advocacy activities across towns and villages have encouraged hundreds of women to register with female farmers’ associations and take up farming, including through home gardening. Their experience highlights the importance of making agricultural financing accessible to women and other groups that may be excluded from conventional farming arrangements. Without affordable credit, the potential contribution of women to Nigeria’s food production drive will remain constrained. Other failed rice project Amidst the failures recorded in rice projects across Northern parts there are other fortune reversals of the Nigerian rice value-chain in other regions that grow the commodity. The government of Chief Martin Elechi in Ebonyi State established modern rice cluster mills in three senatorial districts, located at Izzi, Ikwo and Oso Edda around 2013. The mills started with very big expectation to complement the existing Abakaliki rice mill with morden machines. The mill started simultaneously churning out foreign-like polished rice and with good packaging with the brand name EbonyRice. But the mills have turned to ghosts of themselves as at 2025. A former worker at the mill Mr. Onyeka Ndukwe Nkama, told Vanguard that Governor Elechi’s administration handed over the mills to Chief David Umahi who handed over a dying project to the present administration. The modern mills started closing down one after the other starting from the mill at Oso Edda to Ikwo and now the Izzi mill has finally shutdown. Nkama stated: “The managers had complained of lack of enough Paddy to feed the mills, they said that Ebonyi Rice farmers could not produce enough rice to run three mills. At some time, they were sourcing rice Paddy from the northern part of the country to feed the mills but to no avail. “So, after some time some parts of the machines started rusting and could not perform effectively. So, gradually the mills started packing up. I learnt that the mill at Izzi that worked last but I’m not sure whether it still processing rice. For some time now all the workers at the mills had left to look for other jobs.” Chief Charles Ugwu established a private rice mill at Ikwo which produced high quality rice branded as Ebony Gold and Ebony Silver. The mill has also shut down due to similar Paddy problems. Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief , Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) & Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos) contributed to this report. items.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump pushes board
items.description: Jensen Huang will return as Nvidia’s president and CEO, the company’s board announced Monday, in a stunning reversal for an executive who resigned two weeks ago following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy. The move is effective immediately, the chip giant said in a statement. The company said the board’s unanimous decision to reinstate Huang came after “input from senior levels of the United States government.” President Donald Trump cheered news of Huang’s return in an interview with CNBC and confirmed that he personally intervened to make it happen, speaking “directly and indirectly” with the company’s board — a highly unusual step for an American president. He said he believed the executive “did nothing wrong” and “there’s nothing wrong with a comeback.” In a previous social media post, Trump said the federal government had“no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” Nvidia’s stock soared 31% on the news, buoying the market after a technology sell-off Friday that seemed to confirm anxieties about a bubble in the AI sector. Nvidia’s advanced computer chips power key AI firms’ models, and the company has helped finance the country’s massive investment in new data centers. Huang said in a statement of his own that he was “honored to return to NVIDIA.” Huang has established himself in recent years as the unofficial ambassador for the AI boom, the companies backing it and the trillions of dollars being poured into the sector. Nvidia employees greeted him with loud cheers at the company’s corporate headquarters in Santa Clara, California, on Monday, videos posted online showed. 00:42 Jensen Huang thanks Nvidia for the ‘second chance’ 00:0000:00 “I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support,” Huang said in his statement. The reinstatement was all the more dramatic given that Nvidia’s newly installed chairman, Harvey Jones, effectively dismissed this possibility last week. “The Nvidia Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said in a statement on Nov. 17. In an interview the same day, Nvidia’s interim chief executive Collette Kress also said that the company would not reinstall Huang. Huang’s removal from Nvidia came after The New York Times reported that Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, a woman who U.S. intelligence agencies believed was a Chinese spy. The Financial Times followed that report, saying that Huang had an affair with the woman. In a memo to Nvidia’s workforce Nov. 8, Huang said, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” The New York Times then reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with a senior leader at Nvidia who reported directly to him. The company’s board launched a search for a new leader, reportedly seeking out Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas. However, Haas earlier Monday announced that he was remaining at Arm, with a contract extension through 2033. Nvidia also set up a new “national security and export control oversight” panel in light of the revelations about Huang. Trump, in his social media post, said Attorney General Todd Blanche “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Blanche spoke with Trump over the weekend and told him that the Justice Department had no evidence of any wrongdoing by either Huang or Nvidia, a Justice Department official told NBC News. Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, who serves on the Senate Foreign Relations and Intelligence committees, expressed skepticism about Trump’s assurances. “No national security risk? Based on what?” Cornyn wrote in a post on X . The company could still face legal exposure on other fronts despiteTrump’s statement. The Wall Street Journal and Reuters both reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is probing the company. The Journal said the inquiry was focused on the firm’s accounting practices. The SEC declined to comment to NBC News on Friday. Nvidia did not return a request for comment on the reports. California Attorney General Rob Bonta’s office confirmed Monday it would continue probing Nvidia. “The reinstatement of Jensen Huang does not change the fact that the American people deserve to know what happened here — whether Nvidia misled investors and the public,” Bonta’s office said. Huang’s return likewise “changes nothing” for the three House committees that are set to conduct a closed-door interview with Huang on Dec. 1, a spokesperson for the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence told NBC News. Huang is scheduled to appear before the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. Nvidia’s general counsel is also set to appear Dec. 2. The following day, Huang is scheduled to appear at a public hearing before the Senate Banking Committee on “Protecting America’s AI Advantage.” Huang can expect to face tough questions there from some of his public detractors, and the hearing will be closely watched. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had initially been scheduled to testify alongside Huang, but a Monday notice from the committee listed Huang as the only witness. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with Alice Huang, a businesswoman suspected of being a spy, in 2024. Ann Wang / Reuters Lutnick, reached by phone Monday, told NBC News: “Nice to speak to you. See you.” He then hung up. The ranking Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement: “The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls.” Warren also called for more transparency into how Trump’s input may have played into Nvidia’s decision to bring Huang back. Huang had received an outpouring of support from prominent Silicon Valley tech leaders and investors, many of whom clamored for his return. Brad Gerstner, CEO of Altimeter Capital Management, which has a significant stake in Nvidia, wrote in a letter last week co-authored with Atreides Management managing partner Gavin Baker that Nvidia’s board should keep all options on the table, including potentially asking Huang to return. Yale School of Management professor Jeff Sonnenfeld said the White House’s involvement in Huang’s reinstatement raises serious questions about corporate governance and conflicts of interest, creating “total turmoil and confusion over integrity.” “It looks like a serious erosion of capitalism,” Sonnenfeld said.

items.title: Andrew received £750,000 from Turkish millionaire, court told
items.description: A Turkish millionaire has told the High Court she was misled over a £750,000 payment she made to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor in 2019. Nebahat Isbilen alleges her former business adviser, Selman Turk, misappropriated £38m of her assets, including a payment to the then-Duke of York that she believed was for help with her passport. Turk has rejected the allegations, saying the 81-year-old Isbilen knew the money was paid in the hope that Mountbatten-Windsor could help her husband, a politician in prison in Turkey. Mountbatten-Windsor repaid the £750,000 and is expected to give evidence to the High Court in December. He is not accused of any wrongdoing. Isbilen’s lawyers also told the court on Monday that Turk had instructed a separate £15,000 payment to Mountbatten-Windsor’s ex-wife, Sarah Ferguson, purportedly for the former Duchess of York’s 60th birthday party in 2019, and an unquantified “wedding gift” payment for their daughter Princess Beatrice. Isbilen’s family founded a major soap and cosmetics firm in Turkey. But when her husband, Ilhan, a former member of the Turkish parliament, was arrested in 2015, she wanted help moving her assets out of Turkey. Her lawyers said the charges were “politically motivated” and that in 2017 she was facing “political persecution”. She left Turkey for Greece in 2017 and moved to London in 2018. Simon Colton KC, representing Isbilen, said she met Turk in January 2017 and gave him control of most of her financial assets. But Turk “deliberately and systematically abused” her trust and transferred the money to companies he owned or controlled, Colton added. Colton added that Isbilen approved the £750,000 payment to Andrew, but that Turk “lied to her” about its purpose, which was “a further example of his dishonesty”. The court heard that Isbilen had a private dinner with the then Duke and Duchess of York at Turk’s flat in December 2019 where she discussed her husband’s case. Turk’s lawyers told the court that Isbilen understood and directed her own affairs. Joshua Hitchens, representing Turk, said in written submissions: “In circumstances where the claimant dined with the duke and duchess and discussed her husband with them, she cannot have believed that the £750,000 was a disguised fee for help with a passport, or with a visa.” The trial before Mr Justice Adam Johnson is due to conclude in March, with a written judgment at a later date.

items.title: Gov. Mutfwang loses brother
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed. The Plateau State Government confirmed the death on Monday, as the State Executive Council and the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council paid separate condolence visits to the Governor’s family at the Government House, Jos. The Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, who led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the Governor’s Residence at the Old Government House, Jos, described the deceased as “a distinguished personality, a devoted family man, a lover of peace and a patriotic Nigerian who made meaningful contributions to public service.” She said the Council received the news of his passing “with profound shock and sadness,” noting that his death was “not only a painful loss to the Mutfwang family but also a significant loss to Plateau State and the nation, given his contributions to society and his exemplary life.” Piyo prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked Almighty God to grant the Governor, the bereaved family and all those mourning his demise “the strength, grace and fortitude to bear the tragic loss.” In a separate visit, the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council also condoled with the Governor and his family over the death of Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang. The delegation, led by the Emir of Wase, Alhaji (Dr.) Muhammadu Sambo Haruna, who spoke on behalf of the Council’s Co-Chairman, Rev. Prof. Pandam Yamsat, described the deceased’s passing as “a painful loss to the family and the state.” Haruna acknowledged the inevitability of death as part of the human experience, urging the bereaved family to “find solace in the sovereignty and wisdom of Almighty God.” He also prayed that God would grant the family “the comfort, strength and resilience needed to navigate this difficult period.” Responding on behalf of the family during the separate condolence visits, Mr. Jonathan Mutfwang expressed “profound appreciation to both delegations for their thoughtful gesture, solidarity and prayers.” He noted that their presence had brought “considerable comfort and encouragement to the bereaved family at this difficult time.” Jonathan also prayed for God’s continued protection, blessings and preservation upon members of the delegations. The family disclosed that the burial of the late Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang has been scheduled for Thursday, November 26, 2026. The condolence visits were disclosed in a statement signed by the Director of Press and Public Affairs to the Governor, Gyang Bere, PhD, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Monday. The post Gov. Mutfwang loses brother appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: [Fact-checking] CAN 2025 : l’annonce de Fabrizio Romano sur le verdict du TAS est fausse
items.description: Le célèbre journaliste Fabrizio Romano annonce le Maroc vainqueur de la CAN 2025 en invoquant MARCA. Pourtant, le journal espagnol ne rapporte qu'une anticipation des dirigeants marocains. Le TAS n'a encore tranché pour aucun camp. Décryptage d'une annonce trompeuse. Verdict : FAUX ET TROMPEUR Une publication de Fabrizio Romano, suivie par des millions d'abonnés à travers le monde, a annoncé que le Maroc serait le vainqueur de la CAN 2025 à l'issue de la procédure devant le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS). Pourtant, une vérification de la source invoquée, le quotidien espagnol MARCA, et une confrontation avec le communiqué officiel du TAS révèlent une présentation trompeuse de l'information. À ce stade, aucune décision n'a été rendue en faveur du Maroc. Le verdict est attendu ce mardi 24 novembre, dans l'après-midi. 1. Ce qu'affirme Fabrizio Romano Dans une publication sur sa page Facebook, le journaliste italien Fabrizio Romano annonce : « DÉTAILS : LE MAROC SERA LE GAGNANT DE L'AFCON 2025, MARCA DÉVOILÉE AVANT LE JUGEMENT ». Il ajoute : « L'annonce du directeur du journal espagnol Juan Castro : Le Maroc sera dévoilé comme gagnant de l'AFCON demain. » La publication est accompagnée d'une photographie d'Achraf Hakimi semblant célébrer une victoire. Le choix de cette illustration renforce visuellement le message d'une victoire marocaine déjà acquise, alors même que la décision arbitrale n'est pas encore connue. Cette publication qui a récolté en une heure plus de 147.000 reactions sur la page de Romano, appelle deux observations. D'abord, elle présente comme une certitude ce qui relève, dans l'article de MARCA, d'une anticipation. Ensuite, elle ne distingue pas les informations provenant des sources proches de la Fédération royale marocaine de football (FRMF) d'une éventuelle communication officielle du TAS. Compte tenu de l'audience considérable de Fabrizio Romano, dont la page Facebook compte près de 30 millions d'abonnés selon les chiffres avancés, cette présentation est susceptible de donner une résonance internationale à une information insuffisamment vérifiée. 2. MARCA annonce-t-il réellement une décision favorable au Maroc ? C'est le premier élément à vérifier. Car Fabrizio Romano s'appuie précisément sur le quotidien sportif espagnol. Dans son article consacré au contentieux entre le Sénégal et le Maroc, MARCA écrit : « Selon des sources consultées par MARCA, la décision devrait rester favorable aux Lions de l'Atlas. C'est en tout cas la conviction qui prévaut au sein des instances dirigeantes du football marocain. » Cette formulation est particulièrement importante. Le journal ne dit pas que le TAS a rendu sa décision. Il ne rapporte pas davantage une confirmation émanant du tribunal ou de ses arbitres. Il expose une conviction qui prévaut au sein des instances dirigeantes du football marocain. La nuance est fondamentale : les sources de MARCA semblent être des interlocuteurs proches de la partie marocaine, directement concernée par la procédure. Le quotidien espagnol rapporte donc une anticipation de la FRMF, et non une décision judiciaire dont il aurait eu connaissance. En matière de fact-checking, cette distinction relève d'une règle élémentaire : une source proche d'une partie à un contentieux ne peut être assimilée à une source institutionnelle indépendante. 3. La confrontation avec le communiqué officiel du TAS Le deuxième élément, et sans doute le plus déterminant, est le communiqué publié par le Tribunal arbitral du sport le lundi 23 novembre 2026. L'instance basée à Lausanne annonce explicitement que les parties ont été informées que sa décision sera rendue le mardi 24 novembre, dans le courant de l'après-midi. Le communiqué précise également : « Seules les informations communiquées par les canaux du TAS sont considérées comme officielles, et toute annonce concernant cette affaire sera publiée sur le site Internet du TAS. » Le tribunal ajoute qu'il interrompt toute communication avec les médias concernant cette décision jusqu'à son annonce officielle. Cette communication institutionnelle ne laisse aucune place à l'interprétation : au moment où Fabrizio Romano publie son information, le verdict n'a pas encore été officiellement rendu public. Le TAS ne confirme ni une victoire du Maroc ni une victoire du Sénégal. Il annonce simplement la date à laquelle sa décision sera communiquée. La RTS, dans une publication du 23 novembre, rapporte également cette échéance. Reuters, à travers une dépêche reprise par Africanews, confirme que le verdict est attendu mardi après-midi. 4. Une confusion entre prédiction et information judiciaire Le problème de la publication de Fabrizio Romano réside dans la transformation d'une information conditionnelle en affirmation catégorique. Il faut distinguer trois éléments : Ce que dit MARCA : des sources consultées par le journal indiquent que les responsables marocains sont convaincus d'une issue favorable à leur pays. Ce qu'affirme Fabrizio Romano : le Maroc sera annoncé comme vainqueur de la CAN 2025. Ce que dit le TAS : la décision sera rendue mardi 24 novembre dans l'après-midi. Ces trois formulations ne disent absolument pas la même chose. MARCA rapporte les attentes de responsables marocains. Romano présente ces attentes comme un résultat acquis. Le TAS, seule instance habilitée à trancher ce contentieux, n'a pas encore communiqué le sens de sa décision. Il existe donc un décalage manifeste entre la source initiale et la conclusion diffusée à des millions d'internautes. 5. La photographie d'Achraf Hakimi : une illustration qui renforce la confusion La photographie d'Achraf Hakimi accompagnant la publication mérite également d'être relevée. Dans un contexte où le verdict est particulièrement attendu au Sénégal comme au Maroc, montrer un joueur marocain dans une posture de célébration contribue à installer visuellement l'idée d'une victoire déjà acquise. Or, une photographie de célébration ne constitue évidemment pas une preuve de l'issue d'une procédure arbitrale. Cette mise en scène, associée à un titre catégorique et à la notoriété de Fabrizio Romano, peut entretenir une confusion entre une hypothèse relayée par des sources marocaines et une décision effectivement rendue par le TAS. 6. Ce que l'on sait réellement de la procédure Pour rappel, le Sénégal avait remporté la finale de la CAN 2025, le 18 janvier à Rabat, grâce à un but de Pape Gueye inscrit durant les prolongations. Le 17 mars, la commission d'appel de la CAF avait annulé ce résultat et déclaré le Sénégal forfait, attribuant une victoire administrative de 3-0 au Maroc. La Fédération sénégalaise de football (FSF) avait ensuite saisi le Tribunal arbitral du sport pour contester cette décision. Après l'audience du 8 octobre à Lausanne, les parties sont désormais dans l'attente de la sentence arbitrale. C'est précisément cette décision qui sera communiquée le mardi 24 novembre après-midi. Jusqu'à sa publication, aucune des deux parties ne peut légitimement se prévaloir d'une victoire judiciaire. Conclusion : une information trompeuse qui ne résiste pas à la vérification L'affirmation de Fabrizio Romano selon laquelle le Maroc sera annoncé vainqueur de la CAN 2025 ne repose, dans les éléments présentés, sur aucune confirmation officielle du Tribunal arbitral du sport. Elle est fausse. L'article de MARCA qu'il invoque ne fait état que des convictions de sources issues des instances dirigeantes du football marocain. Il ne rapporte pas un verdict déjà rendu. Le communiqué du TAS publié le 23 novembre apporte la clarification définitive sur le calendrier : la décision sera rendue le lendemain, mardi 24 novembre, dans l'après-midi. Le verdict est donc sans ambiguïté à ce stade : affirmer que le TAS a déjà tranché en faveur du Maroc est faux. Le Maroc peut espérer une décision favorable, le Sénégal peut espérer obtenir gain de cause, mais aucun des deux camps ne connaît encore officiellement l'issue de cette procédure. Dans une affaire aussi sensible, la notoriété d'un journaliste et le nombre de ses abonnés ne sauraient remplacer la vérification des sources. En journalisme, une prédiction, même relayée par un média réputé, ne devient jamais une décision de justice. Par Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.title: La Junta Electoral abre expediente a Silvia Intxaurrondo por posible vulneración de la neutralidad
items.description: La Junta Electoral Central ha abierto un expediente informativo a la presentadora de TVE Silvia Intxaurrondo al entender que unas declaraciones en el programa La hora de La 1 pudieron vulnerar las exigencias de neutralidad informativa. También este lunes, el órgano superior de la administración electoral ha requerido a la Corporación RTVE para que inste “expresamente a doña Silvia Intxaurrondo a que, en el ejercicio de sus funciones como presentadora, observe con el máximo rigor dichos principios, de conformidad con la doctrina reiterada de esta Junta”. La presentadora reflexionó ante la cámara sobre si una televisión pública debía dar cabida a la extrema derecha un día después de la entrevista al líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, en La Revuelta. Tras conocer la apertura del expediente, Intxaurrondo ha asegurado que acudirá a los tribunales. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Book Review: Brianna Wiest’s essay collection is an invitation to embrace self-compassion
items.description: Some books offer advice, while others make readers feel as though someone has finally put their unspoken emotions into words. Brianna Wiest’s “When You’re Ready, This Is How You Heal” belongs to the latter category. Reading this book felt surprisingly personal. At times, it was almost as though Wiest was speaking directly to me, acknowledging feelings and experiences I had struggled to explain. Her words offered a sense of validation, reminding me that pain does not always need to be justified

items.title: Sinner lo intentó, pero perdió el pulso con su rodilla: quirófano, bisturí y más tiempo de baja
items.description: Estaba este 2026 destinado a ser un atracón entre los dos mejores, Alcaraz y Sinner, Sinner y Alcaraz. La realidad, sin embargo, ha sido muy diferente: un solitario cruce que se hizo esperar —abril, en la final del Masters de Montecarlo— y que ya no se produciría más. Primero se detuvo el español, torpedeado por la muñeca, y más adelante tuvo que pisar el freno el italiano, renqueante de una rodilla que finalmente no perdonará. Game, set and match para ella. Lo intentó, pero en esta ocasión no ganó . El de San Cándido apostó por un tratamiento conservador que no termina de funcionarle, de modo que ha optado por pasar por el quirófano, según adelantó Il Giornale y fueron confirmando este lunes los medios de su país. Seguir leyendo AL FINAL, NUEVE TORNEOS DESCARTADOS Hasta que decidió parar, Sinner había ganado este año seis trofeos: cinco Masters 1000 —todos los posibles hasta esa fecha, los nueve del calendario ya tachados en su currículo— y su sexto grande. Es decir, más títulos que nadie, hasta que Alcaraz logró el pasado domingo el cetro maestro e igualó su cifra de éxitos. Precisamente allí, en Turín, Cahill hizo unas declaraciones a Tennis Channel en las que reconocía que para el tenista no estaba resultando nada fácil abordar la situación y toda la incertidumbre. ¿Operarse o no? ¿Cuánto tiempo más estar parado? ¿Cuánto tardará en recuperar el verdadero nivel? “Para él ha sido frustrante estar tanto tiempo alejado de la competición por algo que parecía leve”, indicaba el oceánico, ya jubilado; “pero la actitud con la que está afrontando este proceso es muy admirable. Hace cada día tres o cuatro horas de gimnasio para recuperarse y ganar fuerza en la rodilla”. Desde el 12 de julio, Sinner se ha perdido las siguientes citas: Montreal, Cincinnati, US Open, Pekín, Shanghái, Viena, París y la Copa de Maestros. Quizá también la Davis. En función de cuándo regrese, podría seguir perdiendo una cuantiosa bolsa de puntos; de entrada, los 800 que obtuvo por las semifinales en Australia.

items.title: South-East governors are with me, working for my re-election — Tinubu
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru Ahead of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu on Monday told the Igbo community in Lagos and their leaders that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election. The President said he was excited and that he would go home happy and eat because of their endorsement of his second term. He thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on January 16, 2027. He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians. President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders and leaders of Ndigbo during a town hall meeting organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State. He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous and united Nigeria. To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time. “I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and may God continue to guide and bless our country. It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president. “I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. Though tribes and tongues may differ, in brotherhood we stand. None of us told God where we would be born or what language we would speak when we were born. Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no control over yourself. God created you and created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians. “Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house, geographically called Nigeria,” the President told the gathering. The President said his administration recognises the significant contributions of the Igbo communities to Nigeria’s economic growth, assuring them that no section of the country would be left behind under the Renewed Hope Agenda. President Tinubu appreciated the leadership of all the market leaders in Lagos for leaving their businesses to be at the gathering. “To all of you, I am grateful for one thing: that you are here this afternoon. You left your businesses and money-making opportunities to come and listen to the president, and I must say thank you,” he said. The President expressed his determination to consolidate his administration’s economic gains. He said national development requires collective commitment, mutual understanding and cooperation, urging the Igbo community to embrace dialogue and constructive engagement to address challenges and advance their interests within the Nigerian federation. A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga said: “President Tinubu told the gathering that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.” He mentioned Chief Chidi Anyeagbu, owner of Chisco Motors; Dave Umahi; Doris Uzoka-Anite; and Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who were at the gathering, as people with whom he has close connections. President Tinubu explained some of the reasons behind his policies, such as ensuring that tertiary institutions are no longer paralysed by union strikes. “To eliminate the crisis in the universities, to build good roads and train the engineers who will maintain our cars, our children must be in school. Just because they are poor doesn’t mean they must not go to university or develop. “We are doing that with NELFUND. The university is stable today because we are doing well. We are putting money into agriculture and trading, and anyone in the trade business can apply to the Bank of Industry and get a loan; anyone in agriculture can take a small farmers’ loan. “We have to maintain this country for the sake of every one of us. The critical line in our national anthem is what I’m standing here for. I begged for it, and I am ready to serve. “And I served the first term. The constitution says I can ask for a second term. I want a second term. As you are here today, you make me happy, you make me excited, and I will go home happy and eat akpu,” he said. President Tinubu also called on Ndigbo residents in Lagos to participate actively and vote for him, APC governorship candidate Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. He commended the organisers of the town hall meeting for providing a platform for constructive engagement between the Federal Government and the Igbo community. On his part, the host governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, rallied members of the Ndigbo to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, assuring the President of massive votes from the state in the January 16, 2027, presidential election. Sanwo-Olu described the turnout of Igbo leaders, traders and business owners as proof that Lagos residents were united behind the President, despite the meeting being held on a Monday, when many participants had to leave their businesses to attend. The governor urged the community to sustain the unity and support, saying Lagos would deliver an unprecedented number of votes for Tinubu. He also praised Tinubu as a detribalised Nigerian and nationalist, saying his administration had promoted development across the six geopolitical zones and strengthened national unity. Sanwo-Olu further commended the President for what he described as economic stability, increased investment and opportunities for young people, while thanking him for his contributions to Lagos State. Describing the gathering as a reflection of the “One Lagos” spirit, the governor said the presence of people from different ethnic backgrounds demonstrated that residents could work together in support of a common political cause. In her remarks, the convener of the meeting and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite, declared the Igbo community’s commitment in Lagos State to supporting President Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the community had resolved to unite behind his leadership. She said the Ndigbo had commenced grassroots mobilisation across Lagos State, with structures established at the polling-unit level ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Also speaking, the former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Hon. Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, assured President Bola Tinubu of the Ndigbo’s support for his 2027 re-election bid, saying the gathering of Igbo leaders and stakeholders in Lagos demonstrated their unity and commitment to the President. She said the community had recognised the importance of building political alliances with other geopolitical zones to achieve its future presidential ambition. The leader of the Ndigbo Traders Association in Lagos, Prince Tony Nwakeze, pledged the members’ support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, while appealing for access to loans at a 5 per cent interest rate to help traders transition from importation to local manufacturing. Nwakeze said traders from Alaba, Trade Fair and Ladipo markets were seeking financial support to empower young people and expand their businesses. He also assured the President that traders were prepared to organise themselves and adopt a cross-guarantee arrangement to ensure repayment of any loans granted to their members. He also pledged that the market leadership would honour agreements reached with the government, stressing that traders had learnt from previous misunderstandings and were committed to sustaining a cordial relationship with the Lagos State Government. He thanked the President for attending the meeting and promised that traders across Lagos markets would support him and honour every agreement reached with the government. “We, the market people, will stand with you, support you and honour every agreement we enter into today,” he said. items.title: Tunisie | Zied El Heni sera en grève de la faim le 10 décembre
items.description: Depuis sa cellule, le journaliste Zied El Heni a annoncé avoir officiellement informé l’administration de sa décision d’observer une grève de la faim à l’occasion de la Journée internationale des droits de l’homme, célébrée le 10 décembre. Selon les précisions fournies par le journaliste, ce mouvement de protestation s'inscrit en réaction à ce qu'il qualifie de « mauvais traitements » ainsi que de « procès iniques et simulacres de procès » engagés à son encontre en raison de ses prises de position et de l'exercice de sa profession. À travers cette démarche, Zied El Heni entend également dénoncer les atteintes portées aux libertés publiques, et plus particulièrement à la liberté d'expression, affirme-t-il, en ajoutant que cette grève de la faim constitue un acte de solidarité envers ses confrères détenus, citant nommément Borhen Bsaies, Mourad Zeghidi et Mohamed Youssfi. Y. N. L’article Tunisie | Zied El Heni sera en grève de la faim le 10 décembre est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

Mondial U17 : le Mali, premier africain qualifié pour les seizièmes de finale
items.description: Les Aiglonnets du Mali ont validé leur billet pour les seizièmes de finale de la Coupe du monde U17, lundi, au Qatar. Vainqueurs de la Belgique (2-1), ils signent une deuxième victoire consécutive et assurent leur qualification avant même la dernière journée de la phase de groupes. Le Mali poursuit son parcours avec autorité à la Coupe du monde des moins de 17 ans. Opposés à la Belgique, lundi 23 novembre, dans le cadre de la deuxième journée du groupe G, les jeunes Maliens se sont imposés sur le score de 2 buts à 1. Un succès qui leur permet de décrocher leur qualification pour les seizièmes de finale avant leur dernière sortie en phase de groupes. La rencontre avait pourtant mal commencé pour les Aiglonnets. Les Belges ont ouvert le score dès la 13e minute par l'intermédiaire de Niels Filipo. Mais la réaction malienne ne s'est pas fait attendre. Cinq minutes plus tard, Djigui Koita a remis les deux équipes à égalité (18e). Il a fallu attendre la 67e minute pour voir le Mali prendre définitivement l'avantage. Bien servi par Issiaka Koné, Yaya Niang a inscrit le deuxième but malien, offrant ainsi aux siens une victoire précieuse. Ce résultat confirme le bon début de compétition des jeunes Maliens, déjà vainqueurs de la Nouvelle-Zélande (3-0) lors de leur première sortie. Halidou Maïga, auteur d'un doublé, et Makan Sacko avaient alors permis à leur équipe de réussir son entrée dans le tournoi. Avec six points au compteur, le Mali occupe la première place du groupe G et ne peut plus être rejoint par la Nouvelle-Zélande et le Vietnam, qui comptent chacun un point après deux journées. Les Aiglonnets sont ainsi assurés de terminer parmi les deux premiers de leur groupe et deviennent la première sélection africaine à valider son ticket pour les seizièmes de finale de cette édition. Cette qualification confirme également les ambitions maliennes dans une compétition qui réunit, pour la deuxième année consécutive, 48 sélections. Le format prévoit la qualification des deux premiers de chacun des douze groupes, ainsi que des huit meilleurs troisièmes, pour les seizièmes de finale. Le Mali disputera son dernier match de poule contre le Vietnam avec l'objectif de consolider sa première place. Une nouvelle étape attend ainsi les jeunes Aiglonnets, qui avaient déjà atteint les seizièmes de finale lors de la précédente édition.

items.title: Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence
items.description: The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured. The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice. The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe. According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety. The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety. “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.” Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities. The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms. He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives. items.title: The Economy Is a Hostage Situation
items.description: If there was ever any doubt, it ought to be silenced now. You, me, and Donald Trump—we all live in an Nvidia-state. What you need to know about living in an Nvidia-state is that it is not a democracy. Nor is it ruled by a benevolent king. Instead, the Nvidia-state governs via the logic of a hostage situation. You have two choices: Let AI rip while tech leaders act with impunity, or watch the economy enter a recession. [ Read: ] A scandal at the center of the economy If you don’t believe me, just read the news. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder and CEO, was reinstated today by the company’s board after more than a week of whinging from shareholders, Silicon Valley leaders, and Trump. Huang had resigned in mid-November after allegations that he had had relationships with at least one employee, as well as a client who was allegedly an intelligence asset for the Chinese government. Trump, who was reportedly briefed multiple times about Huang’s affair with the suspected spy, intervened with the board to broker his return. Because we live in an Nvidia-state, one man’s reinstatement was enough to change the trajectory of the entire stock market. Tech stocks, which sold off sharply late last week, rebounded aggressively. Nasdaq-100 futures went up so fast, they briefly halted trading this morning. Nvidia shares jumped 31 percent. The S&P 500 went up 4.7 percent, and the Nasdaq roared up 6.4 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1,463 points. At the time of this writing, all three averages are on pace for their best day in 19 months. The rationale for this rally is that Huang is the central figure of the AI boom—that Nvidia, which powers the AI economy and props it up with the company’s investments, is basically an exoskeleton around Huang. With him, AI progress and U.S. tech leadership can continue apace; without him, the music stops, investor confidence falters, and the AI bubble pops. On November 9, I wrote that, in the eyes of Silicon Valley and Trump, Huang was too big to fail. For 11 days—the window between Huang’s departure and his return—it looked like I was wrong and the shameless era of lol nothing matters in American politics and technology was winding down. Nope! The professed logic of those calling for Huang’s return was nonsensical . The venture capitalists and shareholders argued that American dominance in the AI race against China depended on Huang’s ability to do whatever he pleased. This impunity included allowing Nvidia leeway to potentially skirt U.S. export controls and get chips into China, and sleeping with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. You might be forgiven for missing the genius of the argument. Rather than control chip access to China, what the president and Silicon Valley’s most shameless leaders really seem to want is twofold. First, they—and especially Trump—want the circularly funded, debt-laden AI boom propping up the global economy to continue, in part because many of these AI companies have extremely large financial commitments on the books to keep purchasing chips. Second, they want to set a precedent. Huang’s return is a signal that those driving the AI boom are, in the eyes of the current administration and the market, above the law. To quote the president , “When you’re a star, they let you do it.” Today, the elites got what they wished for. “The mistake has been corrected,” Elon Musk posted on X this morning. The investor Jason Calacanis, a co-host of the podcast All-In , posted , “Daddy’s home!” in reference to Trump stepping in to help the American economy. The hedge-fund manager Bill Ackman argued that “the wisdom of the crowd prevails,” which is an odd way to characterize the president of the United States intervening in a public company’s board meeting to agitate for a personnel change. It’s unclear exactly what Ackman means by “crowd” or even “wisdom.” On November 3, Americans expressed great skepticism at the polls about data centers, the economy, and AI in general. And a YouGov poll from earlier this month revealed that 54 percent of Americans thought that Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, the alleged spy, “has definitely or probably compromised U.S. national security.” (Trump reportedly told Nvidia board members this week that this was not the case.) But as we know now, the Nvidia-state is not a democracy. It doesn’t care that lawmakers in both parties—who will grill the CEO in December when he testifies in front of Congress—are livid about Huang’s reinstatement and publicly questioning Trump’s involvement. The Nvidia-state does not care about potential subpoenas or congressional investigations. It does not care what might come out about Huang, or Nvidia’s dealings with China, or chip smuggling . What the Nvidia-state cares about is the continued reliance of the economy on one industry, one company, and, seemingly, one man. In Nvidia-state, engine of progress drives you . This is how it goes in an AI hostage economy. Progress, economic security, superintelligence, national security, you name it—all of it is dangled as a carrot for citizens. But all of it, including your retirement savings, is contingent, according to those in charge. Any bit of accountability or oversight could cause the whole thing to come crashing down. Progress squandered. Just keep calm and do what we say, and nobody gets hurt .

items.title: COP31 Failed Climate-Displaced Communities
items.description: Click to expand Image Sea level rise encroaches on Kwai Island in Malaita Province, Solomon Islands. © 2025 NowHere Media/Human Rights Watch Leaving the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, I can’t shake the disconnect between the reality of entire communities losing their homes to rising seas and some governments’ apathy and obstruction of the process. The conference ended without consensus on the proposed Antalya Pact—the overarching political agreement for the COP31 climate summit. I am still in awe of Francis, a community leader from Solomon Islands who traveled to Antalya to share his story. “Walande… the birthplace written in my passport, no longer exists,” he told a hushed room. “It is submerged beneath the waves.” His words moved the high-level event’s moderator to tears. COP31’s inability to reach an overarching agreement leaves communities like Walande—and hundreds of other communities that have been forced to relocate—to face consequences of the climate crisis on their own. Despite coordinated calls from civil society, related outcome decisions do not include explicit discussion of displacement and planned relocation, and governments failed to increase funding to help frontline communities adapt. Nor was there recognition of the International Court of Justice’s landmark opinion affirming that governments have human rights obligations to address the climate crisis. I leave Antalya holding both heartbreak and hope: the summit remains a vital space for global solidarity. Alongside partners in the Coalition on Dignified Climate Relocation, we brought frontline leaders, policymakers, and funders together to exchange lessons, and push for rights-respecting national policies and increased funding for communities forced to relocate. After watching our immersive documentary Solwata, several government officials and climate fund directors stepped up, committing to support finance and policies for relocating communities. Official negotiations fell woefully short, and the UN policy process failed to meet the moment in Antalya. But Marshall Islands, Bangladesh, Fiji, Nepal and other forward-thinking governments are proving that another path is possible. Dignified, rights-respecting solutions already exist—and they can be scaled up. Ethiopia, as host of COP32, should learn lessons from Australia and Türkiye’s failures, and center efforts to advance finance for adaptation and loss damage which are vital to protect the rights of climate displaced communities.

items.title: Saint-Louis accueille la 2e conférence internationale sur l’eau
items.description: Du 24 au 26 novembre 2026, la ville Saint-Louis sera au centre des réflexions internationales sur les enjeux liés à l’eau. Chercheurs, universitaires, décideurs publics et experts se retrouveront à l’occasion de la deuxième Conférence internationale consacrée au thème « L’eau dans tous ses états dans un monde globalisé ». Trois jours d’échanges pour explorer des solutions durables face aux défis de l’accès à l’eau, du changement climatique et de la gouvernance des ressources hydriques. L’eau sera au cœur des débats scientifiques et stratégiques à Saint-Louis. À partir de ce mardi 24 novembre, la ville accueillera la deuxième Conférence internationale « L’eau dans tous ses états dans un monde globalisé » une rencontre qui ambitionne de faire converger les connaissances scientifiques, les politiques publiques et les initiatives opérationnelles autour d’une ressource devenue un enjeu majeur de développement. Organisée sous le patronage du ministère de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement, cette rencontre est portée par l’Académie nationale des sciences et techniques du Sénégal (ANSTS) et l’Institut d’études avancées (IEA) de Saint-Louis, avec la participation de plusieurs partenaires nationaux et internationaux, dont l’Université Gaston Berger de Saint-Louis, l’Académie de l’Eau de France, l’Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières et le Programme hydrologique intergouvernemental de l’UNESCO. Dans un contexte marqué par les effets du changement climatique, la dégradation des écosystèmes aquatiques et les inégalités persistantes dans l’accès à l’eau potable et à l’assainissement, cette conférence entend dépasser les constats pour promouvoir des réponses concrètes. L'ambition est notamment de renforcer les passerelles entre la recherche scientifique, la décision politique, l’innovation et les besoins des territoires. Les travaux s’articuleront autour de six grands axes notamment l’eau, les sociétés, la santé et l’équité, l’eau et le développement économique ; les relations entre eau, climat et environnement ; la gouvernance et la coopération ; l’innovation technologique ; ainsi que le financement et les investissements. Autant de problématiques qui concernent directement les pays africains, confrontés à des défis croissants de sécurisation des ressources hydriques. Au programme figurent des sessions plénières de haut niveau, des panels scientifiques, des tables rondes politiques et des ateliers de co-construction de solutions. Un hackathon consacré aux innovations dans le domaine de l’eau viendra également enrichir les échanges. La rencontre prévoit par ailleurs un espace dédié aux doctorants et jeunes chercheurs. Au-delà des communications scientifiques, les organisateurs attendent de cette rencontre des résultats concrets, notamment une Déclaration de Saint-Louis sur l’eau, des notes d’orientation thématiques et une feuille de route africaine pour accélérer la réalisation de l’Objectif de développement durable n°6, relatif à l’accès universel à l’eau potable et à l’assainissement. A travers ce rendez-vous international, Saint-Louis entend ainsi contribuer au débat mondial sur l’avenir de l’eau et renforcer la place de l’expertise africaine dans la recherche de solutions adaptées aux réalités des territoires. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: Parcelles Assainies : un présumé recruteur de migrants déféré au parquet
items.description: Le Commissariat d’arrondissement des Parcelles Assainies a déféré au parquet, le 20 novembre 2026, un individu poursuivi pour trafic illicite de migrants vers l’Espagne. Il est soupçonné d’avoir escroqué plusieurs candidats à l’émigration en leur promettant une traversée maritime contre des sommes comprises entre 400 000 et 600 000 francs CFA. L’affaire fait suite à plusieurs plaintes déposées par des candidats à l’émigration. Selon leurs déclarations, ils avaient remis au mis en cause des montants variant entre 400 000 et 600 000 francs CFA, en contrepartie d’un voyage clandestin vers l’Espagne à bord d’une pirogue devant quitter Saint-Louis. Mais le départ annoncé n’a jamais eu lieu. Après avoir hébergé les candidats dans des bâtiments inachevés, d’abord à Kayar puis à Saint-Louis, le suspect aurait disparu. Il avait ensuite expliqué par téléphone que la traversée était reportée en raison de la présence de la Marine nationale dans la zone, promettant une nouvelle tentative dans les jours suivants. Les investigations menées par les policiers, avec la collaboration des plaignants, ont permis de localiser le suspect aux Parcelles Assainies, où il serait retourné pour recruter de nouveaux candidats. Une descente effectuée à son domicile familial, situé à l’Unité 9, a permis son interpellation. Entendu par les enquêteurs, l’intéressé a reconnu les faits, tout en mettant en cause un complice qui aurait pris la fuite avec les sommes collectées, estimées à près de cinq millions de francs CFA, ainsi que des téléphones portables. Il affirme n’avoir été qu’un simple recruteur et soutient avoir voulu venir en aide à des jeunes de son quartier. À l’issue de sa garde à vue, il a été déféré au parquet. L’enquête se poursuit afin de faire la lumière sur cette affaire et d’identifier l’éventuel complice.

items.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
items.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. items.title: Cinéma : le Grand Prix du FIF Awards 2026 dédié au président Mamadi Doumbouya, plusieurs figures du cinéma africain distinguées à Conakry
items.description: Le Grand Prix du FIF Awards 2026 a été dédié au président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, à l’issue du grand rendez-vous international du cinéma organisé à Conakry du 19 au 21 novembre 2026. La cérémonie de clôture, tenue samedi soir, a également permis de distinguer plusieurs figures du cinéma africain et guinéen, après trois jours de masterclass, panels, formations et rencontres professionnelles. Ouvert le 19 novembre, l’événement a réuni à Conakry des acteurs, réalisateurs, producteurs, institutions culturelles et passionnés du septième art venus notamment de Guinée, du Mali, du Sénégal, du Cameroun, du Nigeria, du Canada et d’autres horizons. La soirée de clôture a débuté par un tapis rouge avant la cérémonie de remise des distinctions. Parmi les personnalités présentes figuraient notamment les actrices Ruth Kadiri, venue du Nigeria, et Hoctavie Mpondo, du Cameroun, ainsi que plusieurs autres professionnels du cinéma africain. Ce rendez-vous est né de la mise en commun de plusieurs initiatives, notamment le FIF Awards et le Salon du cinéma guinéen, qui ont associé leurs efforts pour créer une rencontre de dimension internationale. Pour les organisateurs, l’objectif est de faire de la Guinée un espace de rencontres, de collaboration et de promotion du septième art, tout en offrant davantage de visibilité aux productions et aux talents locaux. « C’est pour la Guinée qu’on est en train de faire la chose » À la clôture, Abdoulaye Traoré, coordinateur du grand rendez-vous, a expliqué que cette initiative repose sur la volonté de dépasser les intérêts individuels au profit d’une ambition commune. « Quand on a pensé à organiser ce festival ensemble, ce n’était pas nous. Quand chacun organisait à un moment, on disait notre structure, mais à un moment, on s’est retrouvé tout de suite, on a dit que c’est pour la Guinée qu’on est en train de faire la chose », a-t-il expliqué. Selon lui, l’union des organisateurs de festivals est indispensable pour faire progresser le cinéma guinéen. « Nous avons voulu que tous les organisateurs de festivals en Guinée se donnent les mains, qu’on arrive à organiser ce grand rendez-vous. Parce que si Abdoulaye Traoré et son équipe seulement l’organisent, on dirait que c’est juste nos talents qu’on cherche à révéler. Mais si on décide de le faire ensemble, c’est pour toute la Guinée et le cinéma guinéen », a-t-il précisé. L’ambition est également d’attirer en Guinée des personnalités de premier plan de l’industrie cinématographique internationale. « La Guinée d’hier, qui avait le cinéma qui soutenait les autres pays, a besoin du monde aujourd’hui pour que son cinéma puisse briller », a déclaré le coordinateur. Il a par ailleurs appelé les professionnels guinéens à davantage de solidarité. « Si le monde entier peut nous aider aujourd’hui, nous encourager comme la Guinée a aidé d’autres personnes hier, il faut que nous soyons sincères entre nous, que nous nous donnions des mains, que nous soyons unis pour le cinéma guinéen, pas dans l’individualité », a-t-il insisté. Abdoulaye Traoré a également rappelé le rôle du cinéma dans la valorisation de l’histoire et de l’identité du pays : « La Guinée est le paradis, la Guinée de la bauxite, la Guinée du diamant, la Guinée de l’or, mais combien de personnes connaissent la vie de la Guinée ? Son histoire ? Qui peut faire découvrir notre Guinée ? » L’ONACIG salue une dynamique collective Présent à la cérémonie, Amara Traoré, directeur général de l’Office national du cinéma et de la cinématographie de Guinée (ONACIG), a salué le travail des organisateurs et la collaboration entre acteurs privés et institutions. Revenant sur les débuts du FIF Awards, il a expliqué les doutes qui entouraient alors la création de cette initiative. « Quand Abdoulaye Traoré était venu pour me dire qu’il fallait que le FIF existe, il y avait tellement de combats, tellement de choses qui se passaient qu’on ne pouvait pas croire que le FIF allait exister. Mais je me suis dit : nous sommes là pour garantir l’écosystème du cinéma en République de Guinée et le FIF existera », a-t-il témoigné. Pour lui, la tenue de l’événement constitue déjà une avancée importante. « Si nous avons aujourd’hui un tapis rouge, il y a des pays qui n’en ont même pas encore. Donc déjà, nous avons un bon début. Ce n’est pas qu’une histoire à raconter, mais nous avons dépassé le cap de rester dans l’ambition, nous en avons atteint l’objectif. Nous avons mené cette marche et nous sommes derrière vous », a-t-il déclaré. Il a rappelé que l’ONACIG ne peut se substituer aux acteurs privés, mais doit contribuer à créer un environnement favorable au développement de l’industrie cinématographique. Au nom du département de la Culture et de l’Artisanat, il a également salué l’engagement du ministre Moussa Moïse Sylla, ainsi que l’appui des partenaires institutionnels et des délégations étrangères présentes à Conakry. Des invités internationaux séduits par la rencontre Parmi les personnalités distinguées figurait l’actrice camerounaise Hoctavie Mpondo, qui a reçu une distinction dans la catégorie consacrée à la bravoure et au leadership féminin dans le cinéma. « Ce prix me montre que j’impacte et que je peux apporter quelque chose. Et surtout qu’on peut échanger, qu’on peut communier parce que nous sommes là pour tout faire ensemble. L’Afrique forme un et ensemble, nous serons plus forts », a-t-elle confié. Elle a également salué l’accueil et l’esprit de fraternité qui ont marqué ces journées, estimant que les échanges entre professionnels peuvent contribuer à renforcer le cinéma guinéen. Dani Kouyaté, parrain de l’événement et récipiendaire d’un prix d’honneur, a lui aussi dressé un bilan positif de la rencontre. « Les échanges étaient très, très positifs d’une façon générale et donc c’est vraiment un bilan très satisfaisant. Nous avons réussi à faire cet événement, notamment avec l’appui des autorités, parce que vous avez vu un peu quand même l’envergure de l’événement était à la hauteur », a-t-il déclaré. Pour lui, cette première expérience doit servir de point de départ : « L’objectif, c’était de mettre le train sur les rails. Le train est sur les rails, le plein est fait, maintenant il faut gazer », a-t-il lancé, appelant à la poursuite de l’accompagnement des autorités et partenaires. Les femmes mises à l’honneur La cérémonie a également valorisé la contribution des femmes à l’industrie cinématographique africaine à travers la catégorie « Bravoure et leadership féminin dans le cinéma ». Parmi les récipiendaires figuraient notamment Hoctavie Mpondo, Ruth Kadiri, Diariou Bah, codirectrice du Centre culturel franco-guinéen (CCFG), Dalanda Kimbeli Barry, Sandra Serveline, Kande Fatoumata, Koni Sylla, Oumou Baldé Diallo, Marie-Louise Sylla, Aminata Sylla, Mariame « Mame Dollars » et Makhissa Ndiaye, entre autres. Sandra Serveline, présidente et cofondatrice du Festival de cinéma Plan d’ensemble à Châteauguay, au Québec, a reçu deux distinctions : le prix Bravoure et leadership féminin dans le cinéma africain et le prix Institution au service du cinéma. Elle a salué cette reconnaissance et réaffirmé son engagement auprès des jeunes créateurs. « Nous travaillons très fort et nous nous sommes engagés, Philippe et moi, et puis toute l’équipe, à continuer à accompagner les jeunes créateurs guinéens et africains dans l’ensemble, à continuer à aimer le cinéma, à se donner, mais surtout à passer à l’action », a-t-elle expliqué. Pendant le festival, son équipe et de jeunes passionnés ont également réalisé en deux jours un film intitulé « Cliché », de la production au montage. Cette expérience, selon elle, a permis de mesurer l’intérêt des jeunes Guinéens pour le cinéma, y compris ceux qui ne sont pas issus du milieu professionnel. « Nous avons compris qu’ils avaient cet engouement, qu’ils étaient intéressés. Il y a un besoin, le besoin est criant et nous nous engageons à porter notre voix de ce côté pour pouvoir accompagner ces jeunes afin qu’ils ne puissent pas baisser les bras », a-t-elle affirmé. Plusieurs figures et institutions distinguées D’autres personnalités ayant contribué à l’histoire et au développement du cinéma africain ont également été honorées. Le prix d’honneur a notamment été attribué au parrain Dani Kouyaté. Parmi les autres figures distinguées figuraient Cheick Oumar Sissoko du Mali, Cheick Doukouré, Moussa Kémoko Diakité, présenté comme un doyen du cinéma guinéen, Kahité Fofana, Mama Keïta, Ahmed Touré du Mali et Sékou Oumar Barry. Dans la catégorie consacrée aux contributions au développement du cinéma, A+ a été distinguée. KPC a, pour sa part, reçu une distinction au titre des meilleurs donateurs. Plusieurs institutions et structures accompagnant le secteur ont également été récompensées, notamment l’ambassade de France, l’ONACIG, le Centre culturel franco-guinéen (CCFG), l’USAG et Heliwood, ainsi que plusieurs organisations et initiatives cinématographiques. « L’Arc d’or », symbole du rendez-vous Abdoulaye Traoré a également présenté l’identité symbolique de ce rendez-vous à travers son trophée, baptisé « l’Arc d’or ». Inspiré de l’arc marquant l’entrée des villes, ce symbole doit traduire la volonté de faire de la Guinée une terre d’accueil pour les professionnels et grandes personnalités du cinéma international. « Nous avons créé l’arc comme trophée et ce sera notre identité festival-rendez-vous. Tout le monde rentre chez nous. Tout le monde sera le bienvenu chez nous », a-t-il expliqué. À travers cette première édition commune, les organisateurs entendent ainsi poser les bases d’une collaboration durable entre les différents acteurs du cinéma. Entre récompenses, rencontres professionnelles, formation et échanges internationaux, le rendez-vous aura permis de mettre en lumière les ambitions du cinéma guinéen et la nécessité de renforcer les partenariats afin de lui offrir davantage de visibilité sur les scènes africaine et internationale.
